Suspension (ta'liq) is common in speech with verbs of knowledge and opinion when they are followed by an interrogative, a negation, the lam of commencement, or the lam of oath. Verbs close in meaning to verbs of knowledge and opinion are also treated as analogous. Al-Radi said in the commentary on al-Tashil: "Sharing with them in this, i.e., in suspension together with interrogation, are: nazara (to look), tafakkara (to reflect), absara (to see), and sa'ala (to ask)." This is like His saying, "They ask when is the Day of Judgement" [al-Dhariyat 51:12]. Since "sal" here takes its first object, it is suspended from the second object, because the cause of suspension is the content of the speech that follows the particle which makes suspension necessary, and this content is not a state of the first object, so it cannot be a second object of a verb which requires two objects. Sibawayh said: "Because it is a speech in which part has operated on part, so it cannot be an independent subject which nothing before it governs." The verbal cause here is a barrier to the governing verb's direct action on its complement, though the verb remains governing it in meaning and implication. So the clause remains in the position of the complement. The interrogative particle, among the other causes of suspension, is stronger in removing the meaning of what follows from the governing verb that requires it, because speech with it is an interrogation and has nothing of the informative. However, the sense of seeking information produced by the interrogative particle is an incidental meaning in the speech, not intended in itself, rather it is a weakening by its occurrence after an informative governing verb, so the interrogation becomes nominal. For that reason the governing verb's operation is nullified only verbally. Your saying "I know whether Zayd stood" indicates by "I know" that what follows is established, so the interrogation becomes nominal, and suspension is evidence of this. If the interrogation remained in its original sense, it would not be valid for its clause to be governed by the suspended verb. Al-Radi said: "The interrogative particle after 'I know' does not indicate the speaker's interrogation, because of the contradiction between 'I know' and 'is Zayd standing?' rather it is merely interrogative. The meaning is: I know what people ask about." From his words it follows that your saying "I know, is Zayd standing?" is said by one who knows something that people are ignorant of or are concerned to know, in contrast to your saying "I know Zayd standing."

Sometimes the interrogation that follows "sa'ala" is a quotation of the wording of the question, so the interrogative clause explains the question clause. Sadr al-Afadil said, regarding al-Hariri's words: "We asked him how you came to us," meaning: we asked him this question. This may apply to this verse.

It is also possible that "sal" be construed as implying the meaning of "qala" (to say), so that its second object is a statement. Thus "sal" is given two objects: one suits the meaning of its own word, and the other suits the meaning of the implied verb.

Al-Taftazani, in his commentary on the Kashshaf, allowed that the clause "kam ataynahum" is an explanation of what is meant by the question, that is: ask them the answer to this question. Al-Sakalkuti said in his gloss on al-Mutawwal: "Then the clause occupies the position of the object, i.e., there is no suspension in the verb."

The author of the Kashshaf allowed that "kam" be informative, so that it begins a new speech, and the verb of asking is cut off from its complement by ellipsis, indicated by what follows, that is: ask them about their condition in thanking God's favour. Thereby the rebuke is achieved. "Kam ataynahum" is then a gradual escalation in rebuke, by the indication of "and whoever substitutes the favour of God." Because it is far-fetched for it to be informative, Abu Hayyan denied this against the author of the Kashshaf and said: it leads to separating the clause containing "kam" from the question clause, although the intended object of the question is the favours.

"Min ayatin bayyinatin" (of clear signs) is the specifying noun of "kam," on which the particle "min" has entered. The particle "min" which governs the specifying noun of interrogative "kam" in the accusative according to its meaning, and which puts the specifying noun of informative "kam" in the genitive by its implied presence, appears in some places explicitly with the implied element. This is because every particle which governs an implied element may have it made explicit, except in certain places such as the implied "an" after "hatta" (until). Al-Radi said: "When the informative and interrogative 'kam' is separated from its specifying noun by a transitive verb, it is obligatory to put the specifying noun in the genitive with 'min,' that is, to make 'min' explicit, so that the specifying noun is not confused with the object, as in His saying: 'How many gardens and springs they left behind' [al-Dukhan 44:25] and 'How many a town We destroyed' [al-A'raf 7:4]." That is, lest it be confused with the object of the intervening verb. Or it is for alerting the hearer from the outset that it is a specifying noun and not an object, to aid the listener's understanding, and that is among the eloquence of the Arabs. In my view, the reason for the appearance of "min" in the case of separation is only the distance of the specifying noun. It has also been said: the appearance of "min" is obligatory with separation by a transitive verb, and permissible with separation by something other than it, as al-Yamani and al-Taftazani in their two commentaries on the Kashshaf transmitted, as quoted by Abd al-Hakim. In al-Kafiya it is said that the appearance of "min" in the specifying noun of informative and interrogative "kam" is permissible; so Ibn al-Hajib stated without qualification. But al-Radi said he did not find evidence for it with interrogative "kam" except with separation by a verb. As for informative "kam," the appearance of "min" is found abundantly without separation. Apparently Ibn al-Hajib did not heed the specific examples which al-Radi cited, and he only took account of the appearance of "min" with the specifying noun, which is the apparent case.

"Ayah" (sign) here means the miracle and the evidence of the truth of the messengers, or the words which indicate the coming of Muhammad ﷺ, for it is a sign for Moses, since he gave news of it centuries earlier, and a sign for Muhammad, upon him be blessings and peace, since the announcement of him preceded his existence by centuries. Describing it as "clear" (bayyinah) on both interpretations is an intensification of the attribute from the verb "bana," meaning "appeared." So the appearance is the appearance of sight in the first interpretation, and the appearance of indication in the second. In this question and its form there is an ellipsis indicated by His saying, "And whoever substitutes the favour of God," the intended sense being: so they substituted it and did not act by it.

His saying "And whoever substitutes the favour of God" is a tadhyil (appended conclusion) to the clause "Ask the Children of Israel how many We gave them," etc. It indicates that the primary object of this threat is the Children of Israel, who are spoken of in "Ask the Children of Israel." It also indicates that the Children of Israel have substituted God's favour, so that the signs given to the Children of Israel are favours upon them; otherwise there would be no relevance in appending the judgement of "whoever substitutes God's favours" to their account. This is something eloquent speakers intend, so that such a phrase in speech serves in place of many sentences, as a wonderful brevity combining the brevity of ellipsis with the brevity of restriction. For it conveys the sense of saying: "How many clear signs We gave them, which were favours upon them, but they did not esteem them as they should be esteemed, so they substituted God's favour with its opposite after its appearance, and so deserved punishment, for whoever substitutes God's favour, God will punish him." It also conveys by this generality a judgement encompassing those intended and others like them. For this reason the mention of such a comprehensive statement after a particular judgement that preceded it is, in essence, an allusion resembling explicit statement. Its parallel is when someone tells you a story and you say: "God deal with the liars thus and thus," meaning that he has lied in what he told you, for otherwise that supplication would have no place upon hearing that story.

The signs are described as favours because, if they are proofs of the Messenger's truth, their being favours is because the proofs of truth are what guide people to accept the Messenger's call with insight, for those who have not followed him, and increase in firmness of faith those who have followed him. He said, "As for those who believed, it increased them in faith" [al-Tawbah 9:124]. By that confirmation the receiving of the law is achieved, in which is the welfare of this world and the next, and that is an immediate and deferred favour. If the signs are the speech which indicates the good tidings of the Messenger, then they are a favour upon them, because they were meant to illuminate the path of guidance for them at the sending of the Messenger, lest they hesitate about his truth after the signs which they were entrusted to preserve have been fulfilled.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 2, verse 211 (part 2 of 2):

As for the substitution (*al-tabdil*, the replacement of one thing with another) in the first sense, it is a substitution of attribute: they turned away from those signs, so the purpose behind them was altered. By their turning away, the signs became a cause of their wretchedness in this world and the Hereafter. For had they not been given to them, it would have been better for them in this world, since they would have remained in a simplicity that brought them closer to doing good than they are after having deliberately chosen obstinacy and aversion, because these two increase them in intentionally committing evil. In the Hereafter as well, because punishment for disbelief depends on the call (to faith) and the manifestation of the miracle. The polytheists resembled them in this substitution by their turning away from the Qur'an and from reflecting on its guidance, or by substitution in the sense that they used those signs for other than their intended purpose, making them causes of delusion. For God did not give their Messenger those signs except to exalt his community, so they relied on that and became careless regarding the religion, and they said: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved ones﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18], and they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days counted﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80].

Substitution (*al-tabdil*) is making one thing a replacement for another, that is, exchanging it for it. It may be an exchange of essence for essence and an exchange of attribute for attribute, as in the saying of Abu al-Shish:

I exchanged the cloak of youth for a worn-out mantle,
and wretched is the recompense of the one who seeks it.

Here he meant the exchange of the state of youth for the state of old age. And as in the saying of al-Nabigha:

I knew her lively and noble, but she was exchanged
for the calves of the wild cows, the young ones that follow their mothers.

The phrase ﴿the blessing of God﴾ is not an instance of placing the apparent noun in the position of a pronoun, such that the original would be: "and whoever substitutes it, that is, the signs, then indeed God is severe in punishment." This is because it is evident that the phrase "the blessing of God" carries a meaning that encompasses the signs and other blessings.

His saying ﴿after it has come to them﴾: the arrival (*al-maji'*) here is a metonymy (*kinaya*) for clarity, witnessing, and firm establishment, because these are among the necessary implications of arrival in common usage.

The punishment has been made to follow the substitution only after this firm establishment, to indicate that it is a substitution made with full awareness,
[Page 293]
not out of ignorance or error, as in His saying, exalted is He, regarding what preceded: ﴿Then they distort it after they had understood it, while they knew﴾ [al-Baqarah: 75].

The object of the substitution (what the blessing was exchanged for) is omitted so that it includes all the forms of substitution: concealing some of it, turning away from some of it, and bad interpretation (*su' al-ta'wil*, misinterpretation).

The punishment arises from the substitution of those blessings in their attributes or in their essences. Substitution occurs only with the intention of opposing them; otherwise it would not be a substitution at all, but rather confirmation and interpretation (*ta'wil*). This differs from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of God for ingratitude?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28], because in that verse nothing preceded that indicates what the blessing is, and nothing there indicates what it was exchanged for, so it was necessary to state explicitly what it was exchanged for. The substituters in that verse are not the same as the substituters in this one, because those are the disbelievers of Quraysh, as evidenced by His saying after it: ﴿and they set up rivals to God﴾ [Ibrahim: 30].

His saying ﴿then indeed God is severe in punishment﴾ is the answer to the conditional clause and its cause (*'illatuhu*), because placing this general ruling as the answer to the condition indicates that whoever fulfils the condition's verb falls within the generality of this answer. The fact that God is severe in punishment is a established and known matter, so its mention was not intended for information, since that is already known. Rather, it is a threat. Thus it is understood that the purpose is to threaten the one who substitutes, and it implies: "God will punish him, because God is severe in punishment." The meaning of the severity of His punishment is that He does not let the transgressor escape, because He is able to punish.

It has also been permitted that ﴿then indeed God is severe in punishment﴾ itself be the answer to the conditional clause, with the "al-" in *al-'iqab* (the punishment) taking the place of the pronoun suffixed to it, meaning: "severe is His punishing him."

The explicit mention of the Divine Name (*ism al-jalalah*) here, although the apparent requirement would be to say "then indeed He is severe in punishment," serves to instil awe in the listener's heart and to cultivate reverence. It also makes this sentence stand independently like a comprehensive saying, since it is in the position of a proverb, a matter that people already know. Punishment (*al-'iqab*) is the painful recompense for a crime and transgression; it is called *'iqab* because it follows (*yu'qibu*) the offence.

[Page 294]

﴿Their worldly life has been made to seem attractive to those who disbelieve, and they mock those who believe. But those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. God provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾

This is a resumption (istinaf, a new sentence that picks up the thread) that returns to the condition of the disbelievers among the Arabs, who are the intended and implied subject of the earlier verses, beginning with His words: ﴿Do they await only that God should come to them in canopies of clouds?﴾ [2:210], and the argument against them in His words: ﴿Ask the Children of Israel﴾ [2:211]. It is a resumption explaining their strange character, which leads them to pay little attention to faith and its people, and to persist in disbelief and its branches, of which the discussion has already spoken. According to Ibn 'Abbas, the intended ones are the leaders of Quraysh. This resumption therefore has the sense of a reason (ta'lil) for their past conditions, and for this reason it is cut off from the preceding sentences, especially since the digression with His words ﴿Ask the Children of Israel﴾ [2:211] and what follows it has come between them.

The intended meaning of "those who disbelieve" is not the People of the Book, whether openly declared or hypocritical, as is transmitted from Muqatil. This is because it is not the Qur'an's usage to refer to them as "those who disbelieve." Moreover, if they were the intended ones, it would have said "their worldly life has been made to seem attractive to them," since they are of the Children of Israel. Also, His words ﴿and they mock those who believe﴾ suit the condition of the polytheists, not the condition of the People of the Book, as will come.

Tazyin (making something seem attractive) is either making a thing an adornment (zayn), or arguing for its being an adornment, because the form tafa'ala comes for making (ja'l) and also for ascribing (nisba), as in ta'lim (teaching), tafsiq (declaring someone a sinner) and tazkiya (declaring someone pure). Zayn means intense beauty.

"The worldly life" (al-hayat al-dunya) is intended to mean what life includes of pleasures, agreeable things and fine states of being. This is a well-known usage of "life" and its synonyms. In a hadith: "Whoever's migration was for a worldly gain that he would obtain..." meaning for the benefits of the world, and this is an elision of a modifier that has become well known.

As for the meaning of the worldly life being made attractive to them, either: what was created as an adornment in the world has taken hold of their souls and their immersion in admiring it has become intense, because adorning things are fine in the eyes of all people, so the disbelievers are not singled out by making them an adornment, as the implication of His words "to those who disbelieve" requires, since the lam (to) indicates exclusivity. Or: the attractiveness of it is promoted in their souls by a satanic call that makes beautiful what is not beautiful, such as poetic syllogisms and lustful fancies. The one who makes attractive according to the first meaning is God, Exalted, except that they excessively turned to adornment. The one who makes attractive according to the second meaning is Satan and his callers.

The agent of tazyin is omitted because the things made attractive to them are many: among them is the creation of some things as fine and marvellous, such as the beauty of persons and sights; among them is the casting into their souls of the goodness of some things that are not good, such as killing a soul; among them is their turning away from whoever calls them to turn to beneficial matters, until their resolve was confined to immersion in apparent beauties beneath which lies shame, were it to appear; among them is their habituation to rushing after pleasures without reflecting on what is in the interest. And other matters, each of which is suitable to be considered the agent of making attractive, literally or customarily. For this reason the mention of this agent has been folded away to avoid prolixity.

[Page 295]

It is also possible that the agent is omitted because of its subtlety, since what makes the world attractive to them is a hidden matter, so its detailed explanation requires a description of their characters, which is what their souls have acquired of attachment to pleasures and other things, from everything that moved them to attach themselves to it through rivalry or imitation, until they were blind to the harms mixed into the pleasures, or to the particular harms concealed behind the beautifying of blameworthy customs. Weakness of resolve, arising from habituation to indulging in seeking agreeable things without restraining the reins of appetites, led them to persist in this. Because of the specificity of this condition to them, and not to the believers, nor to some of the People of the Book, whose religions nurtured in them the resolve to resist the call of blameworthy souls by informing them of the blameworthy qualities contained in those pleasures, and by commanding them to desist from everything with immediate or deferred harm, so that they would strip the pleasures of these harms if they wished to take them, and reject what is purely blameworthy. These were trained in that through glad tidings and warnings, until it became a settled disposition (malaka) in them. For this reason the world was not made attractive to them, because its adornment in their eyes was subject to judgement against it, sometimes affirmative and sometimes negative. Whoever knows what is in an apparently attractive matter of harms and ugliness, its adornment turns into disgrace for him. The making attractive is specified to them, since what is intended by His words "made attractive to those who disbelieve" is their censure and warning against their character. For this reason it was necessary to take the making attractive as an adornment that counts as censure. So it was necessary that what is meant by it is an adornment mixed with what makes that adornment a blemish. Otherwise, the basic making attractive of the worldly life, which calls for desire for what is beautiful, is not blameworthy when it observes what God has commanded to be observed. God, Exalted, said: ﴿Say: who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions?﴾ [7:32].

I have traced the locations of blameworthy adornment and limited them to three types. The first is what is not an adornment at all, neither in essence nor in attribute, because all of it is censure and harm, but it has been made attractive to people through fancies, satanic thoughts and poetic imaginings, such as wine. The second is what is truly an adornment, but has consequences that make it harm and injury, such as fornication. The third is what is an adornment but is surrounded by what turns it blameworthy, such as the support of the wrongdoer. The illustration of all three has come to mind through the verse of Tarafa:

*Were it not for three things, which are part of the life of the young man and of your grandfather,
I would not care when my visitors stand up.*

*Among them is my being first among the reproaching women to a drink of dark red wine, which foams when mixed with water.*

*And the shortening of a rainy day, while the rainy day delights me, with a plump woman beneath the pitched tent.*

*And my charge when the one who is summoned calls, like a lion of the thicket, which you have awakened, the one ready to pounce.*

His words ﴿and they mock those who believe﴾ are conjoined (atf) to the clause ﴿has been made to seem attractive to those who disbelieve﴾ and so on. This is a condition more astonishing than the one before it, namely the condition of extreme delusion. For they did not limit themselves to being captivated by the blossom of the worldly life, but mocked those who did not weave on their loom, namely the believers who abandoned much of the blossom of the worldly life, because the religion guided them to the obligation of abandoning that in certain situations and kinds which contain corruptions.

Sakhar (mockery), with both letters vowelled, is like faraḥ (joy), and the kha' may be vowelled lightly. Its verb is like faraḥa, and sukhriyya is the noun. It is a wonder mixed with contempt for the state that is wondered at. Its verb is intransitive, because it indicates a psychological quality, like 'ajiba (to wonder), and it is transitive with min, a prefixed particle for the one whose state is wondered at, so it is initial (ibtida'iyya) in a meaningful beginning. In the dialect where it is transitive with bi (with), this is weak.

The manner of their mocking of the believers is that they despised their opinion in turning away from pleasures in obedience to the command of the Messenger, and they considered them to have wasted themselves in that and saw that they had lost their shares behind vain illusions. The disbelievers believed that what had passed of their life without blessing had been lost to them, since there is no eternity in this world and no life after it, as the poet said, recited by Shimr:

*A greater fool than one who laps water said to me: leave wine and drink from a cool, sweet spring.*

So the mockery arises from the making attractive of life among them. For this reason it is correct to make the waw (and) indicate a circumstance (hal), to show that the state of making attractive is restricted by the state of mockery, so the two states are concomitant. And a subject (mubtada') is supposed for the clause, that is, "they mock." It has been said that among those whom the disbelievers mocked were Bilal, 'Ammar and Suhayb, and they would say: these wretches have abandoned the world and its good things, and endured hardships seeking what they call the hereafter, which is a worthless thing. Among those who mocked them was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and the hypocrites.

In the verb of making attractive the past tense is used, and in the verb of mockery the present tense is used, to fulfil the two functions: that the meanings of the verb of making attractive are a settled matter among them, because the past indicates realization. And that the meaning of "they mock" is repeated and renewed from them, because the present indicates renewal. It also informs the hearer that what is realized between the two verbs is also continuous, because a matter firmly settled in the soul does not cease to be repeated. And it informs that what is continuous is also realized, because an act is not continuous unless it has taken root in the doer's self and settled in him. So the meaning in the verse is: it was made attractive to those who disbelieve, and the worldly life is made attractive, and they mocked, and they mock those who believe. On this basis, the past in particular was chosen for the verb of making attractive, and the present in particular for the verb of mockery, giving each of the two attributes the verb most fitting to it. Since making attractive was prior in existence and is the origin of mockery, it was given what indicates realization, to show a disposition, and continuity was indicated by implication. Since mockery is consequent upon making attractive, and its repetition increases the blame, because it is not fitting for a man of honour to mock others, it was given what indicates continuity, and realization was indicated by the implication of continuity, because a continuous thing is necessarily realized.

His words ﴿and those who fear God will be above them﴾: by "those who fear God" is meant the believers whom the disbelievers mocked, because those believers were God-fearing. The apparent construction would be "and they are above them," but he turned away from the pronoun to an explicit noun, to prevent the disbelievers from being deceived into thinking that the pronoun refers to them, and adding it to them by falsehood and fabrication, as they did when they heard His words, exalted be He: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza?﴾ [53:19], when the polytheists prostrated and claimed that Muhammad had praised their gods.

So he turned from the pronoun to the explicit for this reason, but it was not with the noun that preceded, namely "those who believe," for the purpose of drawing attention to the excellence of God-fearing and its being a great cause of this superiority. This follows the Qur'an's custom of seizing opportunities for guidance and instruction, to indicate the superiority of the believers over those who disbelieve, and to alert the believers to the obligation of God-fearing, so that it may be the cause of their excelling over those who disbelieve on the Day of Resurrection. As for believers who are not God-fearing, it is not within the purpose of the Qur'an to be concerned with mentioning their condition, so that they remain always between intense fear and little hope. This is the Qur'an's custom in such a context.

The superiority here is a superiority of honour, a metaphor for the extreme of excellence and lordship, just as "below" is borrowed for the condition of the inferior, the subjugated and the enslaved.

It is restricted to the Day of Resurrection to make explicit its perpetuity, because that Day is the beginning of eternal life. If you say: however much or little God-fearing the believers have, they are above those who disbelieve on the Day of Resurrection through faith, and the context is one of honouring the excellence of believers, so it was more appropriate to mention here the description "those who believe." I say: as for the explanation of the excellence of God-fearing which I mentioned, it has other occasions. I say: the verse is an allusion that those who do not fear God do not have their excellence manifest on the Day of Resurrection, but it appears only after that, because the Day of Resurrection is the beginning of the days of recompense. So those who do not fear God do not have their superiority appear to them on that day, and the disbelievers do not perceive it with the senses.

[Page 298]

God, Exalted, said: ﴿So beware of the Fire whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [2:24]. Yes, their excellence appears after the completion of the punishment decreed for them for their sins.

Narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the verse was revealed concerning the chiefs of Quraysh in Makkah, who mocked the poor among the believers and their weak ones. So God informed them that the poor believers are better than they are in the sight of God. God promised the poor provision, and in His saying ﴿God provides for whom He wills﴾ there is an allusion to threatening the polytheists with cutting off their provision from them and the end of their favoured standing.

His saying ﴿God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ and so on is a concluding statement (tadhyil), intended to magnify the honour of the believers on the Day of Resurrection. This is because a concluding statement must be connected to what precedes it. Thus the listener understands from this concluding statement an implied meaning, whose sense is: "And those who had taught fear of God will be above them with a great superiority that description cannot encompass, because it is a superiority bestowed on them from the bounty of God, and the bounty of God has no end." Also, the mockery of those who disbelieved toward those who believed was that they mocked the poor believers for their poverty.

"Reckoning" here means the limiting of quantity, so the negation of reckoning is a negation of knowing the measure of the provision. This figure of speech (kinaya) has become common in the speech of the Arabs, just as it became common among them to say, "They are counted on the fingers," or "Counting encompasses it," as a kinaya for scarcity. From this comes their saying, "A thing that cannot be counted." Therefore it is correct that reckoning is negated here of a matter whose reckoning is not conceivable, namely the superiority.

Qays ibn al-Khatim said:

*Whatever you withhold from me while awake, you have given it to him*
*in sleep, not scattered and not counted.*

[Page 299]

﴿Mankind was one community. Then God sent the prophets as bearers of good news and as warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth, so that it might judge between people concerning what they differed over.﴾

This is a resumptive clause (*isti'naf*, a sentence that begins a new statement while following on from what came before) that explains that the difference of religions was a matter that arose among humankind for a wisdom that required it, and that this was lifted, and that God brought people back to the unity of religion through Islam.

The connection between this verse and what precedes it admits of several aspects. The first: Fakhr al-Din (al-Razi) said: When God Most High explained, in His words ﴿The worldly life has been made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:212), that the cause of the disbelievers' persistence in their disbelief is their exchange of the worldly life for the Hereafter, He explained in this verse that this condition is not specific to those who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), but was present in earlier times as well,

[Page 299 continues]

because people were one community standing upon the truth, and their disagreement was not caused by transgression and envy in the pursuit of worldly life. End of quotation. The clause is then a resumptive clause of explanation (*isti'naf bayani*), comparing what the Muslims encountered with what occurred among the earlier nations.

The second: It is derived from the words of al-Tibi, at His words ﴿Or did you suppose that you would enter Paradise﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:214), that he took from the words of al-Kashshaf that the purpose of His words ﴿Mankind was one community﴾ is to encourage the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the believers to steadfastness and patience in the face of the harm of the polytheists, by mentioning what the earlier nations met their prophets with and the hardships they suffered. End of quotation. The connection on this view lies in the implication of His words ﴿The worldly life has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they mock﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:212), and so on. The clause is then a fresh resumptive clause (*isti'naf ibtida'i*) connected by association.

The apparent view, in my opinion, is that the position of this verse here combines the position of a concluding remark (*tadhyil*) for what precedes it and an introduction to what follows. As for the first, it conveys the state of the past nations: how disagreement arose among them about the truth, for which God made amends by sending messengers in the eras and generations that His wisdom and kindness required, resembling the condition in which the Muhammadan mission arose and what the Messenger and the Muslims encountered from the polytheists.

As for the second, it introduces what follows of the mention of Islam's exclusive guidance to the truth over which the nations differed. This is the meaning of His words ﴿So God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed﴾, up to His words ﴿to a straight path﴾. This is among the features of Islam being the guardian (*muhayman*) over the divine laws that preceded it, and of its being preferred over all religions. This great distinction must be acknowledged, and it must not become a cause of envy toward the Prophet and his community. This is a rebuttal of the envy of the polytheists, who mock those who believed, and of the envy of the People of the Book, which was previously pointed out in His words (Al-Baqarah 2:142), ﴿The foolish among the people will say: What has turned them from their qibla?﴾ up to His words ﴿He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:142).

From the generality of this there results the teaching to Muslims of the history of the phases of religion across the ages of humankind, in comprehensive words concluded by His words ﴿So God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission﴾. If what is meant by their being one community is unity in goodness and truth, which is the preferred view as will come, then God has indicated that people differed, so He sent prophets to them, dispersed, in order to prepare people to enter one general religion. The connection is then established with the phrase ﴿Enter into submission completely﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:208), on the basis that it is addressed to the People of the Book, meaning: enter the religion of Islam, through which God guided the Muslims.

[Page 300]

If, however, what is meant by people being one community is unity in misguidance and disbelief, then God would have alerted them that the sending of messengers occurs to remove the disbelief and misguidance that arise in the centuries of ignorance. Thus those centuries came to an end with the century that was followed by the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ). The verse then serves as a confirmation for the believers, and the connection is established with His words ﴿The worldly life has been made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:212).

The meaning, then, is that Islam guided to a law that gathers all people, making clear the excellence of this religion and the guidance of its adherents to what others were not guided to. Alongside this is the indication that the laws which preceded it were a preparation for it and a familiarizing with it, as we shall explain at His words ﴿So God guided those who believed﴾.

"Mankind" (*al-nas*) is a collective noun with no singular form from its own root, and the definite article in it is for totality (*li'l-istighraq*) without doubt. Here it is for generality, meaning all of humankind, since there is no particular group intended. But it is a customary generality, based on taking into account the majority and disregarding the rare, since it is evident that no era in which good predominated is free of some wicked people, as in the era of prophethood, and no era in which evil predominated is free of some good people, such as Noah, ﴿and none believed with him except a few﴾ (Hud 11:40).

The word *umma*, with a damma on the hamza, is the name for a group whose affair is one. It is derived from *umm* with a fatha on the hamza, which means aim, that is, they aim at one goal. A group becomes an *umma* when they agree in a homeland, a religion, a language, or in all of these.

The adjective "one" (*wahida*) in the verse is for emphasizing the singularity in the word "community" (*umma*), to prevent the assumption that by "community" is meant a tribe, so that one would think the meaning is that people were of one lineage, since *umma* may be applied to those who are gathered by a single ancestry.

The unity here is intended to mean union and sameness in religion, by the context of the consequent clause ("So God sent the prophets") and so on. It is possible that the meaning is: they were one community in truth and guidance, that is, people were upon one creed of truth and monotheism. In this sense al-Tabari transmitted its interpretation from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Jabir ibn Zayd, and it is the view preferred by al-Zamakhshari. Fakhr al-Din said: It is the view preferred by most of the verifying scholars. Al-Qaffal said: The evidence is His words after it, ﴿So God sent the prophets﴾ up to His words ﴿concerning what they differed over﴾, because the consequence of the report about the sending of the prophets upon the preceding clause, and the causal explanation of the sending by His words ﴿so that it might judge between people concerning what they differed over﴾, comprise from that a statement of eloquent concision, which is that people were one community, then the messengers came to them with encouragement and warning, promise and threat, so that they would remain upon the truth, fearing that they would turn away from it once disagreement began to appear. God supported them with the Books so that it might judge between people concerning what they differed over. Therefore it must be that the coming of the messengers was for the purpose of nullifying a disagreement that arose, and that the disagreement requiring the sending of messengers is the disagreement that emerges after agreement upon the truth, as is required by the consequent linkage to the clause ("people were one community") by the particle *fa* (then) in His words ("so God sent the prophets"), and by the explicit words ("so that it might judge between people concerning what they differed over").

For this reason it is necessary to supply: "then they differed" after His words "one community", because the sending was consequent upon disagreement, not upon being one community. On this understanding Ibn Mas'ud read: "People were one community, then they differed, so God sent..." and so on. If what was meant were that they were one community in misguidance, then the sending of prophets would be correctly consequent upon that very state without any supposition. Had the context not diverted from this, it would have been the obvious reading. For this reason Ibn 'Atiyya said: Whoever supposes that the people in the verse were believers supposes "then they differed" in the statement, and whoever supposes them to be disbelievers, the sending of messengers was to them. End of quotation.

This supposition is supported by His words in the verse of Surat Yunus: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, then they differed﴾ (Yunus 10:19), because the apparent meaning is that the purpose of the two verses is one. Also, since here He informed us about people that they were one community, while we see their disagreement, we know that they did not remain in that condition.

The intended purpose of the verse on this interpretation is to alert that monotheism, guidance, and righteousness are the *fitra* (primordial nature) upon which God created people when He made them, as the verse "Am I not your Lord?" (Al-A'raf 7:172) indicates. Nothing veiled it except the indoctrination of error and the promotion of falsehood. God sent prophets to restore the *fitra* to a partial degree, so their guidance varied in methods according to the varying interests, capacities, and severity of the stubbornness. Among the prophets there was one who eased, and among them one who was severe. He sent Muhammad to complete that restoration and to return people to unity upon goodness and guidance. This is the meaning of His words ﴿So God guided those who believed﴾ and so on.

It is also reported from 'Ata' and al-Hasan that the meaning is: mankind was one community agreed upon misguidance and evil. This is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas. On this reading the clause "So God sent the prophets" is coordinated with the apparent wording without any supposition; that is, they were thus, then God sent the prophets. It is then known that the purpose was that they would guide people to the truth through good tidings and warning.

The purpose of the verse on this interpretation is to show that what God sent the prophets with had undergone alteration and disagreement concerning what they were sent with, and that God sent Muhammad with the Qur'an to guide them to what they differed over. Thus the purpose is to demonstrate the excellence of the religion of Islam and its superiority over the other religions by what it contained of clarity and proof.

Whichever meaning is intended, the verb "was" (*kana*) here is used in its basic sense, namely the attribution of its subject, the thing spoken of, to the content of its predicate in past time, and that this has ceased, since people have become divided into two groups: a group upon the truth and a group upon falsehood.

فَإنْ كانَ المُرادُ الوَحْدَةَ في الحَقِّ فَقَدْ حَصَلَ ذَلِكَ في زَمَنٍ كانَ الغالِبُ فِيهِ عَلى النّاسِ الرُّشْدَ والِاسْتِقامَةَ والصَّلاحَ والإصْلاحَ فَلَمْ يَكُونُوا بِحاجَةٍ إلى بِعْثَةِ الرُّسُلِ إلى أنِ اخْتَلَفَتْ أحْوالُهم فَظَهَرَ فِيهِمُ الفَسادُ، فَقِيلَ كانَ ذَلِكَ فِيما بَيْنَ آدَمَ ونُوحٍ ونُقِلَ هَذا عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وقَتادَةَ ومُجاهِدٍ، وقالَ ابْنُ عَطِيَّةَ: قالَ قَوْمٌ: كانَ ذَلِكَ زَمَنَ نُوحٍ، كَفَرَ جُلُّ قَوْمِهِ فَهَلَكُوا بِالطُّوفانِ إلّا مَن نَجّاهُ اللَّهُ مَعَ نُوحٍ، فَكانَ أُولَئِكَ النَّفَرُ النّاجُونَ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً قائِمَةً عَلى الحَقِّ. وقِيلَ: إنَّما كانَ النّاسُ عَلى الحَقِّ حِينَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ الأرْواحَ الَّتِي سَتُودَعُ في بَنِي آدَمَ، فَفَطَرَها عَلى الإسْلامِ، فَأقَرُّوا لَهُ بِالوَحْدانِيَّةِ والعُبُودِيَّةِ، وهو ما في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى في سُورَةِ الأعْرافِ: ﴿وإذْ أخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهم وأشْهَدَهم عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ ألَسْتُ بِرَبِّكم قالُوا بَلى شَهِدْنا أنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ إنّا كُنّا عَنْ هَذا غافِلِينَ﴾ [الأعراف: ١٧٢] ﴿أوْ تَقُولُوا إنَّما أشْرَكَ آباؤُنا مِن قَبْلُ وكُنّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ [الأعراف: ١٧٣]، عَلى أحَدِ تَفاسِيرِ تِلْكَ الآيَةِ، ورُوِيَ هَذا عَنْ أُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ وجابِرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ والرَّبِيعِ بْنِ سُلَيْمانَ. وفي تَفْسِيرِ الفَخْرِ عَنِ القاضِي عَبْدِ الجَبّارِ وأبِي مُسْلِمٍ الأصْفَهانِيِّ أنَّ مَعْنى الآيَةِ ﴿كانَ النّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ في التَّمَسُّكِ بِالشَّرائِعِ العَقْلِيَّةِ عَلى وُجُودِ الخالِقِ وصِفاتِهِ واجْتِنابِ الظُّلْمِ والكَذِبِ، وحُجَّتُهُما عَلى ذَلِكَ أنَّ قَوْلَهُ (النَّبِيئِينَ) جَمْعٌ يُفِيدُ العُمُومَ، أيْ لِأنَّهُ مُعَرَّفٌ بِاللّامِ، فَيَقْتَضِي أنَّ بَعْثَةَ كُلِّ النَّبِيئِينَ كانَتْ بَعْدَ أنْ كانَ النّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً بِدَلِيلِ الفاءِ، والشَّرائِعُ إنَّما تُلُقِّيَتْ مِنَ الأنْبِياءِ، فَتَعَيَّنَ أنَّ كَوْنَ النّاسِ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً شَيْءٌ سابِقٌ عَلى شَرائِعِ الأنْبِياءِ، ولا يَكُونُ إلّا مُسْتَفادًا مِنَ العَقْلِ، وهُما يَعْنِيانِ أنَّ اللَّهَ فَطَرَ الإنْسانَ في أوَّلِ نَشْأتِهِ عَلى سَلامَةِ الفِطْرَةِ (الطبيعة الفطرية السليمة) مِنَ الخَطَأِ والضَّلالِ، قالَ تَعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾ [التين: ٤]. وقِيلَ: أُرِيدَ بِالنّاسِ آدَمُ وحَوّاءُ، نَقَلَهُ ابْنُ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ مُجاهِدٍ وقَوْمٍ. والَّذِي نَجْزِمُ بِهِ أنَّ هَذا كانَ في زَمَنٍ مِن أزْمانِ وُجُودِ النّاسِ عَلى الأرْضِ يَعْلَمُهُ اللَّهُ تَعالى لِقَوْلِهِ ﴿وقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ [الفرقان: ٣٨]، والأظْهَرُ أنَّهُ مِن زَمَنِ وُجُودِ آدَمَ إلى أنْ أشْرَكَ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ. وإنْ كانَ المُرادُ الوَحْدَةَ عَلى الباطِلِ فَقَدْ حَصَلَ ذَلِكَ في زَمَنِ نُوحٍ في أوَّلِ ما قَصَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا، مَعَ ما ورَدَ في الصَّحِيحِ أنَّ نُوحًا أوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ إلى أهْلِ الأرْضِ، فَيَظْهَرُ أنَّ الضَّلالَ
صفحة ٣٠٣
حَدَثَ في أهْلِ الأرْضِ وعَمَّهم عاجِلًا، فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ نُوحًا إلَيْهِمْ، ثُمَّ أهْلَكَ الكافِرِينَ مِنهم بِالطُّوفانِ، ونَجّى نُوحًا ونَفَرًا مَعَهُ، فَأصْبَحَ جَمِيعُ النّاسِ صالِحِينَ، ثُمَّ اخْتَلَفُوا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ.

فَيَجْدُرُ بِنا أنْ نَنْظُرَ الآنَ فِيما تَضَمَّنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ مِنَ المَعْنى في تارِيخِ ظُهُورِ الشَّرائِعِ وفي أسْبابِ ذَلِكَ.

النّاسُ أبْناءُ أبٍ واحِدٍ وأُمٍّ واحِدَةٍ، فَلا جَرَمَ أنْ كانُوا في أوَّلِ أمْرِهِمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً، لِأنَّ أبَوَيْهِمْ لَمّا ولَدا الأبْناءَ الكَثِيرِينَ وتَوالَدَ أبْناؤُهُما، تَألَّفَتْ مِنهم في أمَدٍ قَصِيرٍ عائِلَةٌ واحِدَةٌ خُلِقَتْ مِن مِزاجٍ نَقِيٍّ، فَكانَتْ لَها أمْزِجَةٌ مُتَماثِلَةٌ ونَشَئُوا عَلى سِيرَةٍ واحِدَةٍ في أحْوالِ الحَياةِ كُلِّها، وما كانَتْ لِتَخْتَلِفَ إلّا اخْتِلافًا قَلِيلًا لَيْسَ لَهُ أثَرٌ يُؤْبَهُ بِهِ، ولا يُحْدِثُ في العائِلَةِ تَنافُرًا ولا تُغالُبًا.

ثُمَّ إنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى لَمّا خَلَقَ نَوْعَ الإنْسانِ أرادَهُ لِيَكُونَ أفْضَلَ المَوْجُوداتِ في هَذا العالَمِ الأرْضِيِّ، فَلا جَرَمَ أنْ يَكُونَ خَلَقَهُ عَلى حالَةٍ صالِحَةٍ لِلْكَمالِ والخَيْرِ، قالَ تَعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾ [التين: ٤].

فَآدَمُ خُلِقَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ يَلِيقُ بِالذَّكَرِ جِسْمًا وعَقْلًا، وألْهَمَهُ مَعْرِفَةَ الخَيْرِ واتِّباعَهُ ومَعْرِفَةَ الشَّرِّ وتَجَنُّبَهُ، فَكانَتْ آراؤُهُ مُسْتَقِيمَةً تَتَوَجَّهُ ابْتِداءً لِما فِيهِ النَّفْعُ، وتَهْتَدِي إلى ما يَحْتاجُ لِلِاهْتِداءِ إلَيْهِ، وتَتَعَقَّلُ ما يُشارُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ، فَتَمَيَّزَ النّافِعُ مِن غَيْرِهِ، ويُساعِدُهُ عَلى العَمَلِ بِما يَهْتَدِي إلَيْهِ فِكْرُهُ جَسَدٌ سَلِيمٌ قَوِيٌّ مَتِينٌ. وحَوّاءُ خُلِقَتْ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ يَلِيقُ بِالأُنْثى، خَلْقًا مُشابِهًا لِخَلْقِ آدَمَ، إذْ أنَّها خُلِقَتْ كَما خُلِقَ آدَمُ، قالَ تَعالى: ﴿خَلَقَكم مِن نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ وخَلَقَ مِنها زَوْجَها﴾ [النساء: ١]، فَكانَتْ في انْسِياقِ عَقْلِها واهْتِدائِها وتَعَقُّلِها ومُساعَدَةِ جَسَدِها عَلى ذَلِكَ عَلى نَحْوِ ما كانَ عَلَيْهِ آدَمُ.

ولا شَكَّ أنَّ أقْوى عُنْصُرٍ في تَقْوِيمِ البَشَرِ عِنْدَ الخِلْقَةِ هو العَقْلُ المُسْتَقِيمُ، فَبِالعَقْلِ تَأتّى لِلْبَشَرِ أنْ يَتَصَرَّفَ في خَصائِصِهِ، وأنْ يَضَعَها في مَواضِعِ الحاجَةِ إلَيْها.

هَكَذا كانَ شَأْنُ الذَّكَرِ والأُنْثى، فَما ولَدا مِنَ الأوْلادِ نَشَأ مِثْلَ نَشْأتِهِما في الأحْوالِ كُلِّها. ألَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ اهْتَدى أحَدُ بَنِي آدَمَ إلى دَفْنِ أخِيهِ مِن مُشاهَدَةِ فِعْلِ الغُرابِ الباحِثِ في الأرْضِ، فَكانَ الِاسْتِنْباطُ الفِكْرِيُّ والتَّقْلِيدُ بِهِ أُسَّ الحَضارَةِ البَشَرِيَّةِ.

فالصَّلاحُ هو الأصْلُ الَّذِي خُلِقَ عَلَيْهِ البَشَرُ ودامَ عَلَيْهِ دَهْرًا لَيْسَ بِالقَصِيرِ، ثُمَّ أخَذَ يَرْتَدُّ إلى أسْفَلِ سافِلِينَ. ذَلِكَ أنَّ ارْتِدادَ الإنْسانِ إلى أسْفَلِ سافِلِينَ إنَّما عَرَضَ لَهُ بِعَوارِضَ كانَتْ في مَبْدَأِ الخَلِيقَةِ قَلِيلَةَ الطُرُوِّ أوْ مَعْدُومَتَهُ، لِأنَّ أسْبابَ الِانْحِرافِ عَنِ الفِطْرَةِ السَّلِيمَةِ لا تَعْدُو أرْبَعَةَ أسْبابٍ:
صفحة ٣٠٤
الأُولى: خَلَلٌ يَعْرِضُ عِنْدَ تَكْوِينِ الفَرْدِ في عَقْلِهِ أوْ في جَسَدِهِ، فَيَنْشَأُ مُنْحَرِفًا عَنِ الفَضِيلَةِ لِتِلْكَ العاهَةِ.

الثّانِي: اكْتِسابُ رَذائِلَ مِنَ الأخْلاقِ مِن مُخْتَرَعاتِ قُواهُ الشَّهْوِيَّةِ والغَضَبِيَّةِ، ومِن تَقْلِيدِ غَيْرِهِ بِداعِيَةِ اسْتِحْسانِ ما في غَيْرِهِ مِن مَفاسِدَ يَخْتَرِعُها ويَدْعُو إلَيْها.

الثّالِثُ: خَواطِرُ خَيالِيَّةٌ تَحْدُثُ في النَّفْسِ مُخالِفَةٌ لِما عَلَيْهِ النّاسُ، كالشَّهَواتِ والإفْراطِ في حُبِّ الذّاتِ، أوْ في كَراهِيَةِ الغَيْرِ، مِمّا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ النَّفْسُ، فَيُفَكِّرُ صاحِبُها في تَحْقِيقِها.

الرّابِعُ: صُدُورُ أفْعالٍ تَصْدُرُ مِنَ الفَرْدِ بِدَواعٍ حاجِيَّةٍ أوْ تَكْمِيلِيَّةٍ، ويَجِدُها مُلائِمَةً لَهُ أوْ لَذِيذَةً عِنْدَهُ، فَيُلازِمُها حَتّى تَصِيرَ لَهُ عادَةً، وتَشْتَبِهَ عِنْدَهُ بَعْدَ طُولِ المُدَّةِ بِالطَّبِيعَةِ، لِأنَّ العادَةَ إذا صادَفَتْ سَذاجَةً مِنَ العَقْلِ غَيْرَ بَصِيرَةٍ بِالنَّواهِي رَسَخَتْ فَصارَتْ طَبْعًا.

فَهَذِهِ أرْبَعَةُ أسْبابٍ لِلِانْحِطاطِ عَنِ الفِطْرَةِ الطَّيِّبَةِ، والأوَّلُ كانَ نادِرَ الحُدُوثِ في البَشَرِ، لِأنَّ سَلامَةَ الأبْدانِ وشَبابَ واعْتِدالَ الطَّبِيعَةِ وبَساطَةَ العَيْشِ ونِظامَ البِيئَةِ كُلُّ تِلْكَ كانَتْ مَوانِعَ مِن طُرُوِّ الخَلَلِ التَّكْوِينِيِّ، ألا تَرى أنَّ نَوْعَ كُلِّ حَيَوانٍ يُلازِمُ حالَ فِطْرَتِهِ فَلا يَنْحَرِفُ عَنْها بِاتِّباعِ غَيْرِهِ.

والثّانِي كانَ غَيْرَ مَوْجُودٍ، لِأنَّ البَشَرَ يَوْمَئِذٍ كانُوا عائِلَةً واحِدَةً في مَوْطِنٍ واحِدٍ يَسِيرُ عَلى نِظامٍ واحِدٍ وتَرْبِيَةٍ واحِدَةٍ وإحْساسٍ واحِدٍ، فَمِن أيْنَ يَجِيئُهُ الِاخْتِلافُ.

والثّالِثُ مُمْكِنُ الوُجُودِ، لَكِنَّ المَحَبَّةَ النّاشِئَةَ عَنْ حُسْنِ المُعاشَرَةِ وعَنِ الإلْفِ، والشَّفَقَةَ النّاشِئَةَ عَنِ الأُخُوَّةِ، والمَواعِظَ الصّادِرَةَ عَنِ الأبَوَيْنِ، كانَتْ حَجْبًا لِما يَهْجِسُ مِن هَذا الإحْساسِ.

والرّابِعُ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِالَّذِي يَكْثُرُ في الوَقْتِ الأوَّلِ مِن وُجُودِ البَشَرِ، لِأنَّ الحاجاتِ كانَتْ جارِيَةً عَلى وفْقِ الطِّباعِ الأصْلِيَّةِ، ولِأنَّ التَّحْسِيناتِ كانَتْ مَفْقُودَةً، وإنَّما هَذا السَّبَبُ الرّابِعُ مِن مُوجِباتِ الرُّقِيِّ والِانْحِطاطِ في أحْوالِ الجَمْعِيّاتِ البَشَرِيَّةِ الطّارِئَةِ.

أمّا حادِثَةُ قَتْلِ ابْنِ آدَمَ أخاهُ، فَما هي إلّا فَلْتَةٌ نَشَأتْ عَنِ السَّبَبِ الثّالِثِ، عَنْ إحْساسٍ وِجْدانِيٍّ هو الحَسَدُ مَعَ الجَهْلِ بِمَغَبَّةِ ما يَنْشَأُ عَنِ القَتْلِ؛ لِأنَّ البَشَرَ لَمْ يَعْرِفِ المَوْتَ إلّا يَوْمَئِذٍ، ولِذَلِكَ أسْرَعَتْ إلَيْهِ النَّدامَةُ، فَتَبَيَّنَ أنَّ الصَّلاحَ هو حالُ الأُمَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ، أوْ هو الغالِبُ عَلَيْها.
صفحة ٣٠٥
ويَنْشَأُ عَنْ هَذا الصَّلاحِ والِاسْتِقامَةِ في الآباءِ دَوامُ الِاسْتِقامَةِ في النَّسْلِ، لِأنَّ النَّسْلَ مُنْسَلٌّ مِن ذَواتِ الأُصُولِ، فَهو يَنْقُلُ ما فِيها مِنَ الأحْوالِ الخُلُقِيَّةِ والخَلْقِيَّةِ، ولَمّا كانَ النَّسْلُ مُنْسَلًّا مِنَ الذَّكَرِ والأُنْثى، كانَ بِحُكْمِ الطَّبْعِ مُحَصِّلًا عَلى مَجْمُوعٍ مِنَ الحالَتَيْنِ، فَإنِ اسْتَوَتِ الحالَتانِ أوْ تَقارَبَتا جاءَ النَّسْلُ عَلى أحْوالٍ مُساوِيَةِ المَظاهِرِ لِأحْوالِ سَلَفِهِ، قالَ نُوحٌ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ في عَكْسِهِ: ﴿ولا يَلِدُوا إلّا فاجِرًا كَفّارًا﴾ [نوح: ٢٧]. ومِمّا يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ حالَ البَشَرِ في أوَّلِ أمْرِهِ صَلاحٌ ما نَقَلَهُ في الكَشّافِ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: أنَّهُ كانَ بَيْنَ آدَمَ ونُوحٍ عَشَرَةُ قُرُونٍ عَلى شَرِيعَةٍ مِنَ الحَقِّ.

ثُمَّ كَثُرَتِ العائِلَةُ البَشَرِيَّةُ وتَكَوَّنَتْ مِنها القَبِيلَةُ، فَتَكاثَرَتْ ونَشَأ فِيها مَعَ الزَّمانِ قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا خَواطِرُ مُخْتَلِفَةٌ، ودَبَّتْ فِيها أسْبابُ الِاخْتِلافِ في الأحْوالِ تَبَعًا لِاخْتِلافٍ بَيْنَ حالَيِ الأبِ والأُمِّ، فَجاءَ النَّسْلُ عَلى أحْوالٍ مُرَكَّبَةٍ مُخالِفَةٍ لِكُلٍّ مِن مُفْرَدِ حالَتَيِ الأبِ والأُمِّ، وبِذَلِكَ حَدَثَتْ أمْزِجَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ، وطَرَأتْ عَلَيْها حِينَئِذٍ أسْبابُ الِانْحِطاطِ الأرْبَعَةُ، وصارَتْ مُلازِمَةً لِطَوائِفَ مِنَ البَشَرِ بِحُكْمِ التَّناسُلِ والتَّلَقِّي. هُنالِكَ جاءَتِ الحاجَةُ إلى هَدْيِ البَشَرِ بِبَعْثَةِ الرُّسُلِ، والتّارِيخُ الدِّينِيُّ دَلَّنا عَلى أنَّ نُوحًا أوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ الَّذِينَ دَعَوْا إلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، قالَ تَعالى: ﴿شَرَعَ لَكم مِنَ الدِّينِ ما وصّى بِهِ نُوحًا﴾ [الشورى: ١٣] الآيَةَ. ولَمّا ذَكَرَ الرُّسُلَ في آياتِ القُرْآنِ ابْتَدَأهم في جَمِيعِ تِلْكَ الآياتِ بِنُوحٍ، ولَمْ يَذْكُرْ آدَمَ. وفي حَدِيثِ الشَّفاعَةِ في الصَّحِيحِ تَصْرِيحٌ بِذَلِكَ، أنَّ آدَمَ يَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ يَسْتَشْفِعُونَ بِهِ: إنِّي لَسْتُ هُناكم، ويَذْكُرُ خَطِيئَتَهُ، ايتُوا نُوحًا أوَّلَ رَسُولٍ أرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ إلى أهْلِ الأرْضِ. وبِهَذا يَتَعَيَّنُ أنَّ خَطِيئَةَ قابِيلَ لَيْسَتْ مُخالَفَةَ شَرْعٍ مَشْرُوعٍ، وأنَّ آدَمَ لَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولًا، وأنَّهُ نَبِيءٌ صالِحٌ أُوحِيَ إلَيْهِ بِما يُهَذِّبُ أبْناءَهُ ويُعَلِّمُهم بِالجَزاءِ.

فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى (﴿فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيئِينَ﴾) هو عَلى الوَجْهِ الأوَّلِ مُفَرَّعٌ عَلى ما يُؤْذِنُ بِهِ قَوْلُهُ ﴿كانَ النّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ مَعَ تَحَقُّقِ وُجُودِ الخِلافِ بَيْنَهم بِالمُشاهَدَةِ، مِن إرادَةِ أنَّ كَوْنَهم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً دامَ مُدَّةً ثُمَّ انْقَضى، فَيَكُونُ مُفَرَّعًا عَلى جُمْلَةٍ مُقَدَّرَةٍ تَقْدِيرُها: فاخْتَلَفُوا فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيئِينَ. وعَلى الوَجْهِ الآخَرِ مُفَرَّعًا عَلى الكَوْنِ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً في الباطِلِ، فَعَلى الأوَّلِ يَكُونُ أوَّلُ النَّبِيِّينَ المَبْعُوثِينَ نُوحًا، لِأنَّهُ أوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ لِإصْلاحِ الخَلْقِ، وعَلى الثّانِي: يَكُونُ أوَّلُهم آدَمَ، بُعِثَ لِبَنِيهِ لَمّا قَتَلَ أحَدُهم أخاهُ؛ فَإنَّ الظّاهِرَ أنَّ آدَمَ لَمْ يُبْعَثْ بِشَرِيعَةٍ لِعَدَمِ الدَّواعِي إلى ذَلِكَ، وإنَّما كانَ مُرْشِدًا كَما يُرْشِدُ المُرَبِّي عائِلَتَهُ.

والمُرادُ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ هُنا الرُّسُلُ بِقَرِينَةِ قَوْلِهِ ﴿وأنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الكِتابَ بِالحَقِّ﴾، والإرْسالُ بِالشَّرائِعِ مُتَوَغِّلٌ في القِدَمِ، وقَبْلَهُ ظُهُورُ الشَّرْطِ، وهو أصْلُ ظُهُورِ الفَواحِشِ، لِأنَّ الِاعْتِقادَ الفاسِدَ أصْلُ
صفحة ٣٠٦

ذَمِيمِ الفِعالِ، وقَدْ عَبَدَ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ الأصْنامَ، عَبَدُوا وَدًّا وسُواعًا ويَغُوثَ ويَعُوقَ ونَسْرًا، وهم يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمْ يَزالُوا في مَواطِنِ آدَمَ وبَنِيهِ في جِبالِ نُوذٍ مِن بِلادِ الهِنْدِ كَما قِيلَ. وفي البُخارِيِّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: أنَّ وَدًّا وسُواعًا ويَغُوثَ ويَعُوقَ ونَسْرًا كانُوا مِن صالِحِي قَوْمِ نُوحٍ، فَلَمّا هَلَكُوا أوْحى الشَّيْطانُ إلى قَوْمِهِمْ أنِ انْصِبُوا إلى مَجالِسِهِمُ الَّتِي كانُوا يَجْلِسُونَ أنْصابًا وسَمُّوها بِأسْمائِهِمْ، فَفَعَلُوا فَلَمْ تُعْبَدْ، حَتّى إذا هَلَكَ أُولَئِكَ وتَنَسَّخَ العِلْمُ عُبِدَتْ. اهـ. وقِيلَ كانُوا مِن صالِحِي قَوْمِ آدَمَ. وقِيلَ إنَّ سُواعًا هو ابْنُ شِيثَ، وإنَّ يَغُوثَ ابْنُ سُواعٍ، ويَعُوقَ ابْنُ يَغُوثَ، ونَسْرَ ابْنُ يَعُوقَ. وقِيلَ إنَّهم مِن صالِحِي عَصْرِ آدَمَ ماتُوا، فَنَحَتَ قابِيلُ بْنُ آدَمَ لَهم صُوَرًا، ثُمَّ عَبَدُوهم بَعْدَ ثَلاثَةِ أجْيالٍ. وهَذا كُلُّهُ زَمَنٌ مُتَوَغِّلٌ في القِدَمِ قَبْلَ التّارِيخِ، فَلا يُؤْخَذُ إلّا بِمَزِيدِ الِاحْتِرازِ. وأقْدَمُ شَرِيعَةٍ أثْبَتَها التّارِيخُ شَرِيعَةُ بِرَهَمانَ في الهِنْدِ، فَإنَّها تَبْتَدِئُ مِن قَبْلِ القَرْنِ الثَّلاثِينَ قَبْلَ الهِجْرَةِ.

وفي هَذا العَهْدِ كانَتْ في العِراقِ شَرِيعَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ بِبابِلَ وضَعَها مَلِكُ بابِلَ المَدْعُوُّ حَمُورابِي، ويَظُنُّ المُؤَرِّخُونَ أنَّهُ كانَ مُعاصِرًا لِإبْراهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، وأنَّهُ المَذْكُورُ في سِفْرِ التَّكْوِينِ بِاسْمِ "مَلِكِي صادِقْ" الَّذِي لَقِيَ إبْراهِيمَ في شالِيمَ وبارَكَ إبْراهِيمَ ودَعا لَهُ.

والبَعْثُ: الإرْسالُ والإنْهاضُ لِلْمَشْيِ، ومِنهُ بَعَثَ البَعِيرَ إذا أنْهَضَهُ بَعْدَ أنْ بَرَكَ. والبَعْثُ هُنا مَجازٌ مُسْتَعْمَلٌ في أمْرِ اللَّهِ النَّبِيءَ بِتَبْلِيغِ الشَّرِيعَةِ لِلْأُمَّةِ.

و(النَّبِيِّينَ) جَمْعُ نَبِيءٍ، وهو فَعِيلٌ بِمَعْنى مَفْعُولٍ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنَ النَّبَأِ وهو الخَبَرُ المُهِمُّ، لِأنَّ اللَّهَ أخْبَرَهُ بِالوَحْيِ وعَلِمَ ما فِيهِ صَلاحُ نَفْسِهِ وصَلاحُ مَن يَنْتَسِبُ إلَيْهِ. فَإنْ أمَرَهُ بِتَبْلِيغِ شَرِيعَةِ الأُمَّةِ فَهو رَسُولٌ، فَكُلُّ رَسُولٍ نَبِيءٌ. والقُرْآنُ يَذْكُرُ في الغالِبِ النَّبِيءَ مُرادًا بِهِ الرَّسُولُ. وقَدْ وَرَدَ أنَّ عَدَدَ الأنْبِياءِ مِائَةُ ألْفٍ وأرْبَعَةٌ وعِشْرُونَ ألْفًا، لا يَعْلَمُ تَفْصِيلَهم وأزْمانَهم إلّا اللَّهُ تَعالى، قالَ تَعالى ﴿وَقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ [الفرقان: ٣٨]، وقالَ ﴿وَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِنَ القُرُونِ مِن بَعْدِ نُوحٍ﴾ [الإسراء: ١٧]. وعَدَدُ الرُّسُلِ ثَلاثُمِائَةٍ وثَلاثَةَ عَشَرَ.

والمُرادُ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ هُنا خُصُوصُ الرُّسُلِ مِنهم، بِقَرِينَةِ قَوْلِهِ "بَعَثَ"، وبِقَرِينَةِ الحالِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾، لِأنَّ البِشارَةَ والإنْذارَ مِن خَصائِصِ الرِّسالَةِ والدَّعْوَةِ، وبِقَرِينَةِ ما يَأْتِي مِن قَوْلِهِ ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ الآيَةَ.
[صفحة ٣٠٧]
فالتَّعْرِيفُ في النَّبِيِّينَ لِلِاسْتِغْراقِ، وهو الِاسْتِغْراقُ المُلَقَّبُ بِالعُرْفِيِّ في اصْطِلاحِ أهْلِ المَعانِي.

والبِشارَةُ: الإعْلامُ بِخَيْرٍ حَصَلَ أوْ سَيَحْصُلُ. والنِّذارَةُ بِكَسْرِ النُّونِ: الإعْلامُ بِشَرٍّ وضُرٍّ حَصَلَ أوْ سَيَحْصُلُ، وذَلِكَ هو الوَعْدُ والوَعِيدُ الَّذِي تَشْتَمِلُ عَلَيْهِ الشَّرائِعُ.

فالرُّسُلُ هُمُ الَّذِينَ جاءُوا بِالوَعْدِ والوَعِيدِ. وأمّا الأنْبِياءُ غَيْرُ الرُّسُلِ فَإنَّ وظِيفَتَهم هي ظُهُورُ صَلاحِهِمْ بَيْنَ قَوْمِهِمْ حَتّى يَكُونُوا قُدْوَةً لَهم، وإرْشادُ أهْلِهِمْ وذَوِيهِمْ ومُرِيدِيهِمْ لِلِاسْتِقامَةِ مِن دُونِ دَعْوَةٍ، حَتّى يَكُونَ بَيْنَ قَوْمِهِمْ رِجالٌ صالِحُونَ، وإرْشادُ مَن يَسْتَرْشِدُهم مِن قَوْمِهِمْ، وتَعْلِيمُ مَن يَرَوْنَهُ أهْلًا لِعِلْمِ الخَيْرِ مِنَ الأُمَّةِ.

ثُمَّ هم قَدْ يَجِيئُونَ مُؤَيِّدِينَ لِشَرِيعَةٍ مَضَتْ، كَمَجِيءِ إسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ والأسْباطِ لِتَأْيِيدِ شَرِيعَةِ إبْراهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، ومَجِيءِ أنْبِياءِ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ بَعْدَ مُوسى لِتَأْيِيدِ التَّوْراةِ. وقَدْ لا يَكُونُ لَهم تَعَلُّقٌ بِشَرْعِ مَن قَبْلَهم، كَمَجِيءِ خالِدِ بْنِ سِنانٍ العَبْسِيِّ نَبِيًّا في عَبْسٍ مِنَ العَرَبِ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾. الإنْزالُ حَقِيقَتُهُ تَدْلِيَةُ الجِسْمِ مِن عُلُوٍّ إلى سُفْلٍ، وهو هُنا مَجازٌ في وُصُولِ الشَّيْءِ مِنَ الأعْلى مَرْتَبَةً إلى مَن هو دُونَهُ، وذَلِكَ أنَّ الوَحْيَ جاءَ مِن قِبَلِ اللَّهِ تَعالى ودالٌّ عَلى مُرادِهِ مِنَ الخَلْقِ، فَهو وارِدٌ لِلرُّسُلِ في جانِبٍ لَهُ عُلُوُّ مَنزِلَةٍ.

وأضافَ "مَعَ" إلى ضَمِيرِ "النَّبِيِّينَ" إضافَةً مُجْمَلَةً، واخْتِيرَ لَفْظُ "مَعَ" دُونَ "عَلَيْهِمْ" لِيَصْلُحَ لِمَن أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كِتابٌ مِنهم، مِثْلِ إبْراهِيمَ ومُوسى وعِيسى ومُحَمَّدٍ، ولِمَن جاءَ مُؤَيِّدًا لِمَن قَبْلَهُ، مِثْلِ أنْبِياءِ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ بَيْنَ مُوسى وعِيسى.

والكِتابُ هو المَكْتُوبُ، وأُطْلِقَ في اصْطِلاحِ الشَّرْعِ عَلى الشَّرِيعَةِ، لِأنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ النّاسَ بِكِتابَتِها لِدَوامِ حِفْظِها والتَّمَكُّنِ مِن مُدارَسَتِها. وإطْلاقُ الكِتابِ عَلَيْها قَدْ يَكُونُ حَقِيقَةً إنْ كانَتِ الشَّرِيعَةُ في وقْتِ الإطْلاقِ قَدْ كُتِبَتْ أوْ كُتِبَ بَعْضُها، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى ﴿الم ذَلِكَ الْكِتَابُ﴾ [البقرة: ١] عَلى أحَدِ الوَجْهَيْنِ المُتَقَدِّمَيْنِ هُنالِكَ، وقَدْ يَكُونُ مَجازًا عَلى الوَجْهِ الآخَرِ. وما هُنا يُحْمَلُ عَلى الحَقِيقَةِ، لِأنَّ الشَّرائِعَ قَدْ نَزَلَتْ وكُتِبَتْ، وكُتِبَ بَعْضُ الشَّرِيعَةِ المُحَمَّدِيَّةِ.

والمَعِيَّةُ مَعِيَّةٌ اعْتِبارِيَّةٌ مَجازِيَّةٌ، أُرِيدَ بِها مُقارَنَةُ الزَّمانِ، لِأنَّ حَقِيقَةَ المَعِيَّةِ هي المُقارَنَةُ في المَكانِ، وهي المُصاحَبَةُ. ولَعَلَّ اخْتِيارَ المَعِيَّةِ هُنا لِما تُؤْذِنُ بِهِ مِنَ التَّأْيِيدِ والنَّصْرِ، قالَ تَعالى ﴿إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَى﴾ [طه: ٤٦]، وفي الحَدِيثِ: "ومَعَكَ رُوحُ القُدُسِ".

والتَّعْرِيفُ في الكِتابِ لِلِاسْتِغْراقِ، أيْ: وأنْزَلَ مَعَ النَّبِيِّينَ الكُتُبَ الَّتِي نَزَلَتْ كُلَّها.
[صفحة ٣٠٨]
وهُوَ مِن مُقابَلَةِ الجَمْعِ بِالجَمْعِ عَلى مَعْنى التَّوْزِيعِ، فالمَعْنى: أنْزَلَ مَعَ كُلِّ نَبِيءٍ كِتابَهُ، وقَرِينَةُ التَّوْزِيعِ مَوْكُولَةٌ لِعِلْمِ السّامِعِينَ لِاشْتِهارِ ذَلِكَ.

وإنَّما أفْرَدَ الكِتابَ ولَمْ يَقُلِ الكُتُبَ، لِأنَّ المُفْرَدَ والجَمْعَ في مَقامِ الِاسْتِغْراقِ سَواءٌ، وقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ، مَعَ ما في الإفْرادِ مِنَ الإيجازِ ودَفْعِ احْتِمالِ العَهْدِ، إذْ لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يَنْزِلَ كِتابٌ واحِدٌ مَعَ جَمِيعِ النَّبِيِّينَ؛ فَتَعَيَّنَ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ الِاسْتِغْراقَ لا العَهْدَ. وجَوَّزَ صاحِبُ الكَشّافِ كَوْنَ اللّامِ لِلْعَهْدِ، والمَعْنى: أنْزَلَ مَعَ كُلِّ واحِدٍ كِتابَهُ.

والضَّمِيرُ في ﴿لِيَحْكُمَ﴾ راجِعٌ إلى الكِتابِ، فَإسْنادُ الحُكْمِ إلى الكِتابِ مَجازٌ عَقْلِيٌّ، لِأنَّهُ مُبَيِّنُ ما بِهِ الحُكْمُ، أوْ فِعْلُ "يَحْكُمُ" مَجازٌ في البَيانِ.
ويَجُوزُ رُجُوعُ الضَّمِيرِ إلى اسْمِ الجَلالَةِ، أيْ: أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ الكِتابَ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهم، وإسْنادُ الحُكْمِ مَجازٌ عَقْلِيٌّ، لِأنَّهُ المُسَبِّبُ لَهُ والآمِرُ بِالقَضاءِ بِهِ. وتَعْدِيَةُ "يَحْكُمُ" بِـ"بَيْنَ" لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يُعَيَّنْ فِيهِ مَحْكُومٌ لَهُ أوْ عَلَيْهِ.

وحُكْمُ الكِتابِ بَيْنَ النّاسِ بَيانُ الحَقِّ والرُّشْدِ والِاسْتِدْلالِ عَلَيْهِ، وكَوْنُهُ فِيما اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ كِنايَةٌ عَنْ إظْهارِ الحَقِّ، لِأنَّ الحَقَّ واحِدٌ لا يُخْتَلَفُ فِيهِ إلّا عَنْ ضَلالٍ أوْ خَطَأٍ، ولِهَذا قالَ جُمْهُورُ عُلَمائِنا: إنَّ المُصِيبَ في الِاجْتِهادِيّاتِ واحِدٌ.

* * *

﴿وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ فَهَدَى اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِهِ وَاللَّهُ يَهْدِي مَن يَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

عَطْفٌ عَلى جُمْلَةِ ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ لِبَيانِ حَقِيقَةٍ أُخْرى مِن أحْوالِ اخْتِلافِ الأُمَمِ، وهو الِاخْتِلافُ بَيْنَ أهْلِ الكِتابِ بَعْضِهِمْ مَعَ بَعْضٍ، وبَيْنَ أهْلِ الكِتابِ الواحِدِ مَعَ تَلَقِّيهِمْ دِينًا واحِدًا. والمَعْنى: وأنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الكِتابَ بِالحَقِّ فاخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ، كَما قالَ تَعالى ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ فَاخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ﴾ [هود: ١١٠].

والمَعْنى: وما اخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إلّا أقْوامُهُمُ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا كُتُبَهُمْ، فاسْتَغْنى بِجُمْلَةِ القَصْرِ عَنِ الجُمْلَةِ الأُخْرى لِتَضَمُّنِ جُمْلَةِ القَصْرِ إثْباتًا ونَفْيًا.
[صفحة ٣٠٩]
فاللَّهُ بَعَثَ الرُّسُلَ لِإبْطالِ الضَّلالِ الحاصِلِ مِن جَهْلِ البَشَرِ بِصَلاحِهِمْ، فَجاءَتِ الرُّسُلُ بِالهُدى، فاتَّبَعَهم مَنِ اتَّبَعَهم فاهْتَدى، وأعْرَضَ عَنْهم مَن أعْرَضَ فَبَقِيَ في ضَلالَةٍ. فَإرْسالُ الرُّسُلِ لِإبْطالِ الِاخْتِلافِ بَيْنَ الحَقِّ والباطِلِ، ثُمَّ أحْدَثَ اتِّباعُ الرُّسُلِ بَعْدَهُمُ اخْتِلافًا آخَرَ، وهو اخْتِلافُ كُلِّ قَوْمٍ في نَفْسِ شَرِيعَتِهِمْ.

والمَقْصُودُ مِن هَذا بَيانُ عَجِيبِ حالِ البَشَرِ في تَسَرُّعِهِمْ إلى الضَّلالِ، وهي حَقِيقَةٌ تارِيخِيَّةٌ مِن تارِيخِ الشَّرائِعِ، وتَحْذِيرُ المُسْلِمِينَ مِنَ الوُقُوعِ في مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ.

والتَّعْرِيضُ بِأهْلِ الكِتابِ، وهم أشْهَرُ أهْلِ الشَّرائِعِ يَوْمَئِذٍ، فِيما صَنَعُوا بِكُتُبِهِمْ مِنَ الِاخْتِلافِ فِيها. وهَذا مِن بَدِيعِ اسْتِطْرادِ القُرْآنِ في تَوْبِيخِ أهْلِ الكِتابِ، وخاصَّةً اليَهُودَ، وهي طَرِيقَةٌ عَرَبِيَّةٌ بَلِيغَةٌ، قالَ زُهَيْرٌ:
إنَّ البَخِيلَ مَلُومٌ حِينَ كانَ ولَكِنَّ الجَوادَ عَلى عِلّاتِهِ هَرَمُ
[أي: إنَّ البَخِيلَ مَلُومٌ حينَ يكونُ بَخِيلًا، لكنَّ الكريمَ مع عيوبِه الطارئة هرِمٌ (أي: مُسِنٌّ مُتعَبٌ)، والمعنى أنَّ الكريمَ يُمدَحُ ولو تعثَّر.]

وقالَ الفَرَزْدَقُ يَمْدَحُ الخَلِيفَةَ ويَسْتَطْرِدُ بِهِجاءِ جَرِيرٍ:
إلى مَلِكٍ ما أُمُّهُ مِن مُحارِبٍ ∗∗∗ أبُوهُ ولا كانَتْ كُلَيْبٌ تُصاهِرُهُ

والضَّمِيرُ مِن قَوْلِهِ ﴿فِيهِ﴾ يَجُوزُ أنْ يَعُودَ إلى الكِتابِ، وأنْ يَعُودَ إلى الحَقِّ الَّذِي تَضَمَّنَهُ الكِتابُ، والمَعْنى عَلى التَّقْدِيرَيْنِ واحِدٌ، لِأنَّ الكِتابَ أُنْزِلَ مُلابِسًا لِلْحَقِّ ومُصاحِبًا لَهُ، فَإذا اخْتُلِفَ في الكِتابِ اخْتُلِفَ في الحَقِّ الَّذِي فِيهِ، وبِالعَكْسِ، عَلى طَرِيقَةِ قِياسِ المُساواةِ في المَنطِقِ.

والِاخْتِلافُ في الكِتابِ ذَهابُ كُلِّ فَرِيقٍ في تَحْرِيفِ المُرادِ مِنهُ مَذْهَبًا يُخالِفُ مَذْهَبَ الآخَرِ في أُصُولِ الشَّرْعِ لا في الفُرُوعِ، فَإنَّ الِاخْتِلافَ في أُصُولِهِ يُعَطِّلُ المَقْصُودَ مِنهُ.

وجِيءَ بِالمَوْصُولِ دُونَ غَيْرِهِ مِنَ المُعَرِّفاتِ لِما في الصِّلَةِ مِنَ الأمْرِ العَجِيبِ، وهو أنْ يَكُونَ المُخْتَلِفُونَ في مَقْصِدِ الكِتابِ هُمُ الَّذِينَ أُعْطُوا الكِتابَ لِيُزِيلُوا بِهِ الخِلافَ بَيْنَ النّاسِ، فَأصْبَحُوا هُمْ سَبَبَ خِلافٍ فِيهِ. ولا شَكَّ أنَّ ذَلِكَ يُبْطِلُ المُرادَ مِنهُ.

والمَعْنى: تَشْنِيعُ حالِ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ، بِأنْ كانُوا أسْوَأ حالًا مِنَ المُخْتَلِفِينَ في الحَقِّ قَبْلَ مَجِيءِ الشَّرائِعِ، لِأنَّ أُولَئِكَ لَهم بَعْضُ العُذْرِ، بِخِلافِ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا بَعْدَ كَوْنِ الكِتابِ بِأيْدِيهِمْ.

وقَوْلُهُ ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِـ"اخْتَلَفَ"، والبَيِّناتُ جَمْعُ بَيِّنَةٍ، وهي الحُجَّةُ والدَّلِيلُ.
[صفحة ٣١٠]
والمُرادُ بِالبَيِّناتِ هُنا الدَّلائِلُ الَّتِي مِن شَأْنِها الصَّدُّ عَنِ الِاخْتِلافِ في مَقاصِدِ الشَّرِيعَةِ، وهي النُّصُوصُ الَّتِي لا تَحْتَمِلُ غَيْرَ مَدْلُولاتِها، أعْنِي قَواطِعَ الشَّرِيعَةِ، والظَّواهِرَ المُتَعاضِدَةَ الَّتِي التَحَقَتْ بِالقَواطِعِ، والظَّواهِرَ الَّتِي لَمْ يَدْعُ داعٍ إلى تَأْوِيلِها ولا عارَضَها مُعارِضٌ.

والظَّواهِرُ المُتَعارِضَةُ الَّتِي دَلَّ تَعارُضُها عَلى أنَّ مَحْمَلَ كُلٍّ مِنها عَلى حالَةٍ لا تُعارِضُ حالَةَ مَحْمَلِ الآخَرِ، وهو المُعَبَّرُ عَنْهُ في الأُصُولِ بِالجَمْعِ بَيْنَ الأدِلَّةِ، وتَوارِيخِ التَّشْرِيعِ الدّالَّةِ عَلى نَسْخِ حُكْمٍ حُكْمًا آخَرَ (naskh: النَّسْخُ أي إلغاءُ حكمٍ بحكمٍ لاحقٍ)، أوْ ما يَقُومُ مَقامَ التّارِيخِ مِن نَحْوِ: هَذا ناسِخٌ، أوْ كانَ الحُكْمُ كَذا فَصارَ كَذا. فَهَذِهِ بَيِّناتٌ مانِعَةٌ مِنَ الِاخْتِلافِ لَوْ كانَ غَرَضُ الأُمَمِ اتِّباعَ الحَقِّ. ومَجِيءُ البَيِّناتِ بُلُوغُ ما يَدُلُّ عَلَيْها، وظُهُورُ المُرادِ مِنها.

والبَعْدِيَّةُ هُنا بَعْدِيَّةُ اعْتِبارٍ، لَمْ يُقْصَدْ مِنها تَأخُّرُ زَمانِ الِاخْتِلافِ عَنْ مَجِيءِ البَيِّناتِ، وإنْ كانَ هو كَذَلِكَ في نَفْسِ الأمْرِ، أيْ أنَّ الخِلافَ كانَ في حالَةٍ تَقَرَّرَتْ فِيها دَلائِلُ الحَقِّ في نُفُوسِ المُخْتَلِفِينَ.

وقَوْلُهُ ﴿بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ مَفْعُولٌ لِأجْلِهِ لِـ"اخْتَلَفُوا"، والبَغْيُ: الظُّلْمُ. وأصْلُ البَغْيِ في كَلامِ العَرَبِ الطَّلَبُ، ثُمَّ شاعَ في طَلَبِ ما لِلْغَيْرِ بِدُونِ حَقٍّ، فَصارَ بِمَعْنى الظُّلْمِ مَعْنًى ثانِيًا، وأُطْلِقَ هُنا عَلى الحَسَدِ، لِأنَّ الحَسَدَ ظُلْمٌ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّ داعِيَ الِاخْتِلافِ هو التَّحاسُدُ، وقَصْدُ كُلِّ فَرِيقٍ تَغْلِيطَ الآخَرِ، فَيُحَمِّلُ الشَّرِيعَةَ غَيْرَ مَحامِلِها لِيُفْسِدَ ما حَمَلَها عَلَيْهِ الآخَرُ، فَيُفْسِدُ كُلُّ فَرِيقٍ صَوابَ غَيْرِهِ، وأمّا خَطَؤُهُ فَأمْرُهُ أظْهَرُ.

وقَوْلُهُ ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِقَوْلِهِ ﴿بَغْيًا﴾ لِلتَّنْصِيصِ عَلى أنَّ البَغْيَ بِمَعْنى الحَسَدِ، وأنَّهُ ظُلْمٌ في نَفْسِ الأُمَّةِ، ولَيْسَ ظُلْمًا عَلى عَدُوِّها.

Know that the two elements, the prepositional phrase *min ba'di ma jā'athumu* (after the clear proofs had come to them) and the object of purpose *baghyan* (out of rebellion), are both attached to the verb *ikhtalafa* (they differed). This verb is restricted by the exceptive construction (*al-istithnā' al-mufarragh*, the "emptied" exception, in which the excepted item is not explicitly stated). It follows that both elements are restricted to the subject of the verb they are attached to. Therefore the disagreement that al-Radī (Radī al-Dīn al-Astarābādhī) mentioned among the grammarians, concerning whether two things may be excepted after a single exception particle, does not apply here. The reason is that the correct view is that what is involved here is not the exception of multiple things, but the exception of one thing, namely "those who were given it" (*alladhīna ūtūhu*). However, this exception is qualified by two restrictions: *"after the clear proofs had come to them"* and *(baghyan)*, "out of rebellion."

(p. 311)

The intended meaning is that the disagreement did not occur between the people of the religion and its opponents, nor did it occur among the people of the religion before the evident proofs that turn people away from disagreement had appeared, nor was that disagreement based on a good aim. Rather, it occurred among the people of one religion, while the proofs were in place, and it was driven by rebellion and envy.

The verse also requires warning the Muslims against falling into what the earlier nations fell into, namely disagreement in religion, that is, in the foundations of Islam. The disagreement that exists among the scholars of Islam is not a disagreement over the foundations of the Sharī'ah, since these are agreed upon (*ijmā'iyyah*). They have unanimously agreed that they seek to realize these foundations. For this reason their principles agree in investigating the intent of God the Exalted and the Sunnah of His Messenger, in order to infer the aim of the Lawgiver and his dispositions. They agreed on most of the subsidiary rulings (*furū'*), and they differed only in determining the method of arriving at the aim of the Lawgiver. They have been careful about the religion, and they have all declared: God the Exalted has a ruling in every matter; it is one ruling; He has obligated the jurists (*mujtahidīn*, scholars who exercise independent reasoning) to reach it; the one who is correct is one; the one who errs has less reward than the one who is correct; and negligence in seeking it is a sin.

Therefore the disagreement that exists among our scholars is a disagreement of great stature that broadens perspectives. But if their followers came and defended their opinions while it is clear that the basis of their evidence is weak or mistaken, aiming to promote a school of thought and to discredit the opinion of others, then that resembles the disagreement that God the Exalted condemned and warned us against. So be cautious lest you be like it, and do not be like the words of al-Ma'arrī (Abū al-'Alā' al-Ma'arrī, the poet):

*Here is a disputant who has pursued argument, while knowing*
*that the truth in it is not as he claims.*
*The discerning youth knows that insights*
*have become blind, so how often is certainty concealed, and how often is it made blind.*

God's saying *﴿fa-hadā llāhu alladhīna āmanū﴾* ("then God guided those who believed"): this conjunction may be read as *fa-* coordinating with *ikhtalafa fīhi* (they differed concerning it), which is contained in the restrictive clause. Ibn 'Arafa said: "It is conjoined with *fa-*, indicating the speed of His guidance of the believers immediately after the disagreement." End of quotation. He means that the sequence is measured according to what fits the speed of such a matter. Otherwise, the guidance of the Muslims occurred after long periods had passed, until the disagreement of the Jews and the disagreement of the Christians grew severe, and this has a distance that is not hidden. So in my view the apparent meaning is that the *fa-* is *faṣīḥah* (explanatory, marking an implied prior clause), because it is known that the purpose of the preceding discourse is the warning against falling into disagreement. It is necessary that the Qur'an was sent for the guidance of the Muslims to the truth in everything about which the people of the earlier scriptures differed. So it is as if the listener awaited knowledge of the outcome of this disagreement, and it was said: this disagreement continued until Islam came, *then God guided those who believed*, and so on. The *fa-* thus makes explicit a discourse that is implied, namely the conjoined element that is omitted, as in His saying, the Exalted: *﴿Strike the rock with your staff﴾, so it burst forth* (Q. 2:60).

(p. 312)

By "those who believed" is meant, without doubt, the Muslims. The pronoun in *ikhtalafū* refers to all who disagreed, both those who disagreed about the truth before the coming of the messengers and those who disagreed about the laws after the coming of the messengers and the clear proofs. For this reason He clarified it "from the truth," which is the truth mentioned earlier in His saying: *﴿and He sent down with them the Book in truth﴾* (Q. 2:213). The disagreement of both groups returns to disagreement over determining the truth, either out of ignorance or out of envy and rebellion.

*Al-idhn* (permission) means the address granting permission to perform an act. Its origin is derived from the verb *adhina*, when one lends his ear to the speech of someone who addresses him. Then it was applied, figuratively, to the address granting permission to perform an act, by the relation of necessary association, because listening to the speech of a speaker entails attending to him and responding to his request. This usage became widespread until *al-idhn* became more common in the meaning of granting permission to perform an act. Thus the word *al-idhn* came to be capable of being used figuratively for various meanings resembling permissive address. In this verse it is applied metaphorically to enabling guidance and facilitating it through what the laws contain of clarification of guidance and direction toward the means of being guided, because whoever facilitates something for you is as if he has permitted you to take it.

In this there is an indication that God sent Islam to return people to the truth and to the monotheism they had held, or to return them to the truth that the messengers came to achieve. Their followers then differed about it, instead of realizing through their understanding the aims of what their messengers had brought. Through what Islam contains of the clarification of the Qur'an, *which falsehood does not approach from before it or from behind it* (Q. 41:42), the clarity of the truth and the direction toward how to take it were achieved. Thus the coming of Islam completed the purpose of what had been revealed of the earlier laws.

His saying *﴿And God guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾* (Q. 2:213) is a concluding statement (*tadhyīl*) explaining that God's bounty gives it to whom He wills. This is a summary statement, and its detail is that the wisdom of God required that the completion of guidance be delayed until the time of the coming of the law of Islam, because humanity had been prepared, through the coming of the earlier laws, to accept this law. The earlier laws were a preparation and a readying for accepting the religion of Islam. For this reason this verse began with His saying: *﴿Mankind was one community﴾* (Q. 2:213). Just as humanity at the beginning was one community upon simple guidance, then misguidance overtook it when human thoughts were stirred, humanity returned to one religion at a time when thoughts had advanced. This is a remarkable unity, because it came after the scattering of opinions and doctrines. For this reason God the Exalted said: *﴿Indeed, the religion with God is Islam. And those who were given the Book did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rebellion among themselves﴾* (Q. 3:19).

(p. 313)

In a hadith: "The example of the Muslims, the Jews, and the Christians is like a man who hired people to work for him for a day until night, for a known wage. They worked for him until midday, and they said: 'We have no need of your wage that you stipulated for us, and what we have done is void.' He said to them: 'Do not do that; complete the rest of your work and take your wage in full.' But they refused and left. He hired others after them and said to them: 'Complete the rest of this day, and you will have the wage I stipulated for them.' They worked until the time of the afternoon prayer, then they said: 'What we have done is void, and the wage you set for us is yours.' He said to them: 'Complete the rest of your work, for only a little of the day remains.' But they refused. He hired a people to work for him the rest of their day, and they worked the rest of their day until the sun set, and both groups completed their wage. That is their example, and the example of what they accepted of this light.' The Jews and the Christians said: 'We have more work and less reward.' He said: 'Have I wronged you in any of your rights?' They said: 'No.' He said: 'That is My bounty, which I give to whom I will.'"

﴿Or did you suppose that you would enter Paradise without the like of what came to those who passed away before you? Misfortune and hardship touched them, and they were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When will God's help come?" Surely God's help is near.﴾

This is a transitional digression (*idrab intiqali*, a shift away from the previous discourse), so it required a point of connection (*munasabah*) to what precedes it. Al-Tibi said, taking from the words of al-Kashshaf: God's saying ﴿Mankind was one community﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213] is a statement in which the earlier nations are mentioned, along with the prophets sent to them and the hardships they suffered at their hands. It also incorporates an encouragement for the Messenger and the believers to be steadfast and patient in the face of the harm of the polytheists, as He said: ﴿And We relate to you the news of the messengers, by which We strengthen your heart﴾ [Hud: 120]. From this perspective, the Messenger and his companions are intended by that discourse, as indicated by His saying ﴿God guided those who believed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213]. This is what the digression turns away from, through the word "bal" (rather), which is implied by "am" (or). That is: leave that aside; did they suppose they would enter Paradise? End of quotation.

Its explanation: the purpose of mentioning the earlier nations wherever it occurs in the Qur'an is admonition, advice, and warning against falling into what they fell into through their evil deeds, and emulation in praiseworthy conduct. So God's saying ﴿Mankind was one community﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213] and what follows is a general summary of that. It concludes with His saying ﴿God guided those who believed to the truth concerning what they differed about, by His permission﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213]. Since this conclusion is a distinction (*manqabah*) for the Muslims,

[p. 314]

they were alerted not to take pride in this praise, lest they suppose they had fulfilled the due of gratitude for the blessing. Therefore it is followed by the statement that they must be patient with what may confront them on the path of their faith of hardship and adversity, emulating the righteous among the earlier nations. Just as God warned them against falling into what the misguided of those nations fell into, He here urges them to emulate the guided among them, in keeping with the Qur'an's practice of following glad tidings with warning and vice versa. Thus God's saying ﴿Or did you suppose﴾ is a turning away from His saying ﴿God guided those who believed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213], and this serves to console them for what befell them on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah: the polytheists' overbearing conduct toward them in preventing them from performing the 'umrah, and the conditions they imposed upon them for the following year. It also serves as a preparation for His saying ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216] and what follows. It has been related from most of the early exegetes that this verse was revealed concerning the Battle of the Trench, when the Muslims were struck by what afflicted them of hardship and severe trial. That incident would then add to the appropriateness of the connection.

"Am" (or) in the sense of digression is like "bal" (rather), except that "am" indicates interrogation, and here the interrogation serves to affirm the matter and to deny it if it were to occur. That is: rather, did you suppose you would enter [Paradise] without trial? This is a false supposition that should not be held.

*Hasiba* (he supposed), with the *sin* vowelled with a kasra in the perfect, is a verb of the heart, a sister of *zanna* (he thought). In its imperfect there are two forms: with a kasra on the *sin* (*yahsibu*), which is better, and with a fatha (*yahsabu*), which is more regular. Both have been read in the widely known recitations. Its verbal noun is *hisban* with a kasra on the *ha'*. Its origin is from *hisab* (reckoning) in the sense of counting. It was then used for supposition, by way of analogy: the mind's movement in deducing knowledge of what will occur is likened to the hand's movement among objects in order to determine their number. Similar to this is the verb *'adda* (he counted) in the sense of *zanna*.

The address is to the Muslims. It is a turning toward them with direct address after the discourse had been about others, so it contains no *iltifat* (shift of grammatical person).
