It is permissible that His saying ﴿And whether you show﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾ [al-Baqarah: 283], and that His saying ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is an interposed parenthetical between them.

Showing (ibda') what is in the self means making it apparent; it is declaring it by speech in matters whose path is speech, and by action in matters that entail action. Concealing it is the opposite of that. The conjunction of ﴿or conceal it﴾ is for an ascent (taraqqi) in the reckoning concerning it. It has come according to what the apparent sense requires, in conjoining the stronger to the weaker, in the purpose toward which the speech is directed in the context of affirmation. And ﴿mā﴾ (whatever) in the context of negation generalizes to good and evil.

Reckoning (muḥāsaba) is derived from ḥusbān, which is counting. So the meaning of ﴿yuḥāsibkum﴾ (will call you to account) in the original linguistic sense is: He counts it against you. However, its use became common for its necessary consequence, which is holding to account and recompense, as Allah the Exalted related: ﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 113]. This usage became common in the technical terminology of the Shari'ah, and His saying here clarifies it: ﴿then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾.

Allah, exalted is He, has here stated in general terms the states of those who are forgiven and those who are not forgiven, so that believers may be between fear and hope, and not fall short in pursuing good deeds, both inward and practical. However, He affirmed forgiveness and punishment in a general way for each of what we manifest and what we conceal. Among the scholars there are views on the meaning of this verse and on reconciling it with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him," and his saying: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper to them." The best statement on this is what harmonizes the words of al-Mazari and 'Iyad in their commentaries on Sahih Muslim, and it is, with additional clarification: What occurs in the self, if it is merely a passing thought and hesitation without resolve, then there is no disagreement that one is not held accountable for it, since the responsible person has no capacity to turn it away; this is the subject of the hadith of overlooking for the community what their souls whisper to them. If resolve has welled up in the self, then it is either among the thoughts that are followed by bodily acts or not. If it is among the thoughts that are not followed by acts, such as belief, disbelief, and envy, then there is no disagreement that one is held accountable for it, because it falls within the capacity of the responsible person to turn it away from himself. If it is among the thoughts that have effects in the external world, then if the effects occur, it has passed from the state of thoughts into the state of deeds, as with one who resolves to steal and then steals. If he resolves to do it and then gives it up by his own choice, without any obstacle having prevented him, then there is no disagreement that he is not held accountable for it, and this is the subject of the hadith: "Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him." If he gives it up due to an obstacle that compelled him to give it up, then there are two opinions regarding being held accountable for it. That is, His saying ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾ is taken to mean that He will recompense you. And it is general, clarified by the occasions of reward and punishment in many Shari'ah texts. As for those among the early generation (salaf) who called this abrogation (naskh), they followed a usage that preceded the systematization of the technical terms of legal theory (usul al-fiqh), so they applied the term naskh to the meaning of clarification (bayan). This is common in the expressions of the earlier scholars. These hadiths, and what the principles of the Shari'ah's rules indicate, are the clarification of "whom He wills" in His saying: ﴿then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that this verse was abrogated by the one that follows it, namely His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286], as will come there.

With this it has become clear that the willing here is conditioned upon the states of what is shown and what is concealed, as is evident.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿fayaghfir﴾ and ﴿wayu'adhdhib﴾ with jazm (apocopation), in conjunction with ﴿yuḥāsibkum﴾ (will call you to account). Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, Abu Ja'far, and Ya'qub read them with raf' (nominative), as a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), with the assumed phrase "fa-huwa yaghfiru" (so He forgives). Both are eloquent readings, and naSb (accusative) is permissible but was not read with it except in an anomalous reading (shadhdh).

His saying ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾ is a concluding phrase (tadhyil) for what indicated the generality of knowledge, with what indicates the generality of power.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 2, verse 285:

﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return."﴾

Al-Zajjaj said: When Allah mentioned in this surah many rulings and stories, He concluded them with His saying: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord﴾, glorifying His Prophet ﷺ and his followers, and as an emphasis and a summation (fadhlaka) of all that was mentioned before. He means that this is a transition from admonitions, guidance and legislation, and what lies between them that serves those aims, to the praise of His Messenger and the believers for their belief in all of that, a pure belief from which action branches out; for belief in the Messenger and the Book requires compliance with what he brought in terms of action. So the sentence is a fresh, initial resumption (istinaf ibtida'i), placed in this position because of its relevance to what preceded. It is a transition that signals the end of the surah, for when it moved from related topics to another topic that is like the outcome and summation, it indicated that it had fully covered those topics.

It is reported in the context of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) that His saying ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284], as mentioned just before.

The "al" in "al-Rasul" (the Messenger) is for specific reference (al-'ahd), and it became by predominance a proper name for Muhammad ﷺ at the time of revelation. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They plotted to expel the Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah: 13]. "Al-Mu'minun" (the believers) is conjoined (ma'tuf) to "al-Rasul," and the pause is on it.

Here "al-Mu'minun" is a title for those who responded to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so making it the subject of the verb (amana) has a benefit, whereas there is no benefit in your saying: "qama al-qa'imun" (the standing ones stood).

His saying ﴿Each one believes in Allah﴾ is a collective statement after the detailed enumeration. This is the usual manner of "kull" when it comes after the mention of several items regarding a ruling, and then the intent is to collectivize them in that, as in the words of al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas al-Lihbi, after some verses:

"Each one has an intention of hatred toward his companion; by the grace of Allah we bring you forth and you bring us forth."

Since "kull" is one of the nouns that always require an annexed genitive (idafa), when the annexed noun is omitted it takes nunation as a substitute for a singular noun, as Ibn Malik noted in al-Tashil. It is not an objection that "kull" is an inflected noun, for nunation may serve both purposes, so it is a case of using one thing in two senses. Whoever permits "al-Mu'minun" to be a conjunction of sentences, making "al-Mu'minun" a subject, and "kull" a second subject, with "amana" as its predicate, has deviated from the Arabic sense.

Al-Jumhur read "wa kutubihi" in the plural form of kitab, while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "wa kitabihi" in the singular form, meaning the Qur'an or the genus of the Book; it is then equivalent to "wa kutubihi," since the intent is the genus. The truth is that the singular and the plural are equal in denoting the genus. Do you not see that they say: the plural in what follows the genus "al" is nominal (suwari), and for this reason it is said: when the genus "al" enters a plural, it cancels from it the meaning of plurality; likewise every noun intended as a genus, like the annexed noun in these two readings, and annexation comes for what the "al" comes for.

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that when he was asked about this reading, "kitabihi" is more comprehensive than "kutubihi," or "al-kitab" is more comprehensive than "al-kutub," he said that the scope of the singular noun intended as a genus is greater than the scope of the plural when it is intended as a genus, because of the possibility of intending the genus of the pluralities, so the ruling does not extend to what is below the number of the plural among the individuals of the genus. For this reason the author of al-Miftah said: the generalization (istighraq) of the singular is more inclusive than the generalization of the plural. The truth is that the Arabs do not intend this in negating the genus, nor in its generalization in affirmation; and that the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, if its transmission from him is sound, its interpretation is that it is more comprehensive because it is equal to it in meaning while being shorter in wording, so perhaps he meant by "more comprehensive" the more preponderant and stronger meaning.

His saying ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ was read by the majority with the first-person plural "nun" (nun of the speaker who is associated with others). It may admit of a shift (iltifat), being part of a quoted speech of an omitted saying indicated by the context, and "wa qalu" (and they said) is conjoined to it; or the "nun" in it is for majesty, i.e., they believed in a state in which We had commanded them to do so, because We do not distinguish; so the sentence is parenthetical (mu'taridah). It was also said that it is a quoted speech of an omitted saying indicated by "amana," because belief is conviction and speech. Ya'qub read it with "ya" (the third person), so that the pronoun refers to ﴿Each one believes in Allah﴾.

The distinction here is intended as distinction in belief in Him and in affirmation: that one believes in some and disbelieves in others.

His saying ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾: the discussion of its counterpart has already been given under His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿We make no distinction between any of them, and we are submitting to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 136].

﴿And they say, "We hear and we obey"﴾ is conjoined to ﴿The Messenger believes﴾. Hearing here is a metaphor for acceptance, consent and compliance; its opposite, "la yasma'un" (they do not hear), means they do not obey. al-Nabigha said:

"The reciters warned against it because of its bad hearing."

That is: its non-compliance with the incantation.

The meaning: they believed, were reassured, and complied. The past tense was used rather than the present so as to indicate the firmness of that, because they intended to establish acceptance and consent, and formulas of contracts and the like occur in the past tense, such as: "I sold."

"Ghufranaka" is in the accusative as an absolute object: i.e., "forgive a forgiveness from You," so it is a substitute for its verb. "Al-masir" (the final return) may be taken literally, in which case it is an acknowledgment of resurrection, and it is made to end at Allah because it ends at a day or a world in which the power of Allah becomes manifest necessarily. It may also be a metaphor for the completion of compliance and belief, as if they had been runaways before Islam, then they came to Allah. This is like His saying: ﴿So flee to Allah﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 50]. Making the return to Allah a figure for the return to His command and prohibition is like His saying: ﴿and found Allah there, and He paid him his account in full﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. The fronting of the prepositional phrase ("ilayka") serves to express restriction: i.e., the return is to You and not to other than You. This is a true restriction (qasr haqiqi), with its necessary consequence intended, namely that they know they will return to Him, and will not return to other than Him among those whom the people of misguidance worship.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 2, verse 286 (part 1 of 3):

﴿Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It shall have what it has earned, and it shall bear what it has merited.﴾ The more apparent view is that this is part of the words of Allah the Exalted, not part of the quoted speech of the Messenger and the believers. It would then be an interjection (i'tiraḍ) between the clauses introduced by "say." Its purpose is to show the fruit of faith, submission and obedience. Allah thereby informs them that in this religion He has not imposed on them any obligation that involves hardship. Along with this, it is a good tidings of the answering of their supplication, which was taught to them or inspired in them: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes…﴾ up to His words ﴿…that which we have no strength to bear﴾, before He relates those supplications.

It is also possible that this is part of the words of the Messenger and the believers, as if it were a justification of their saying ﴿We hear and we obey﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285]. That is, they understood the meaning of the words of their Lord ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284] to mean that they would be taken to account for what is within their capacity, whether what they showed or what they concealed. This is what appears outwardly in action by choice, or what the heart resolves upon and is at peace with. However, His words ﴿It shall have what it has earned﴾ etc. make this unlikely, since they have no means of establishing that.

As for the view that it is the words of Allah, then it is an abrogation (naskh, the replacement of a ruling by a later one) of His words ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284]. This is related in Sahih Muslim from Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When the verse ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284] was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah. They came to him and said, 'We cannot bear it.' The Prophet said: 'Say: We hear and we obey and we submit.' So Allah planted faith in their hearts. When they did that, Allah abrogated it and revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity.﴾" The use of the term "abrogation" for this is a convention of the earlier scholars, and what is meant is clarification and specification. What the soul finds reassuring is that these verses are consecutive in their arrangement. Nevertheless, it is possible that they were revealed in installments, and that between the periods of revelation something happened which some of the Muslims considered a hardship.

The word "wus'" (capacity) in the Qur'an is pronounced with a damma on the waw. In Arabic speech it may be pronounced with fatha, kasra or damma on the waw, and it means power and ability. Here it means what can be borne and what is within one's ability. It is thus the use of the verbal noun to mean the object (ism al-maf'ul). What is within one's ability (mustata') is what people are customarily able to do if their will is directed to doing it, with soundness and the absence of impediments.

This is evidence that no obligation beyond capacity occurs in the religions of Allah the Exalted, because of the generality of "soul" (nafs) in a negative context. Allah the Exalted did not legislate obligation except for action and the rectification of people's conditions, so He does not burden them with what they cannot do. What has come of such burdens is in the context of punishments. This is a general ruling in all the revealed laws.

The Islamic law is distinguished by ease and gentleness, as attested by His words ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78] and His words ﴿Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185]. For this reason, one of the general principles of jurisprudence is: hardship brings facilitation. Hardship is the basis for dispensation. The determination of the hardships that remove the obligation of worship is mentioned in the principles of jurisprudence, and I have elaborated on this in my book called (Maqasid al-Shari'ah, The Objectives of the Sacred Law). Those obligations that are burdensome are rare, occurring only in times of necessity, such as the obligation on one Muslim to stand firm against ten polytheists at the beginning of Islam when the Muslims were few.

This issue is the one titled in the books of the two foundations (usul, i.e., the principles of jurisprudence and of theology) as the question of obligation to the impossible (al-taklif bi'l-muhal) and obligation to what cannot be borne (al-taklif bi-ma la yutaq). It is an issue on which the books of the Ash'arites and the Mu'tazilites resounded, and they differed over it with a famous difference, prompted by each party's commitment to the necessary implications of their principles and rules.

The Ash'arites said: It is permissible for Allah to impose the obligation of what cannot be borne, based on their rule denying that it is obligatory for Allah to do what is best (al-salah), and that everything that proceeds from Him, exalted is He, is just, because He is the owner of His servants. It is also based on their rule that He, exalted is He, creates whatever He wills, and based on their rule that the fruit of obligation is not limited to the intention of compliance, but may be for the purpose of incapacitating and testing, and making compliance a sign of felicity and non-compliance a sign of wretchedness, and the incurring of sin. For Allah the Exalted may reward the disobedient and punish the obedient. Therefore, punishing one who commands him to do something impossible or unachievable is all the more permissible. They used as evidence the hadith about the obligation upon the image-maker to breathe the spirit into the image when he is not one who breathes it, and the obligation upon the one who lies in a dream to tie two barley grains together when he does not do so. There is no evidence in this, because this is in matters of the Hereafter, and because these two are solitary reports (khabar al-ahad), by which the foundations of religion are not established.

The Mu'tazilites said: The obligation of what cannot be borne is impossible, based on their rule that it is obligatory for Allah to do what is best and to be free of injustice, and their rule that He, exalted is He, does not create reprehensible acts, and their rule that the fruit of obligation is compliance. Otherwise it would become futile, and futility is impossible for Allah. It is also impossible for Allah to punish the obedient or reward the disobedient.

They used as evidence this verse and the verses that indicate its foundations, such as ﴿Your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], ﴿We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15], ﴿Say: Indeed, Allah does not command immorality﴾ [al-A'raf: 28], and so on.

The truth is that what led to delving into this issue was the debate over the creation of the acts of the servants. When al-Ash'ari denied the power of the servant and spoke of acquisition (kasb), explaining it as the coincidence of the servant's power with the occurrence of the act that is willed, without his power being effective in it, the Mu'tazilites compelled him to affirm that Allah had obligated the servants with what is not within their power, which is an obligation of what cannot be borne. So al-Ash'ari accepted that. Imam al-Haramayn, al-Ghazali and al-Ash'ari, however, disagreed on the permissibility of imposing what cannot be borne. The verse does not serve as a proof for either side's position on whether this is possible.

Then those who permitted it differed as to whether it has occurred. Al-Qurtubi related a consensus (ijma') that it has not occurred, and this is the correct report. Imam al-Haramayn said in al-Burhan: "All the obligations, according to al-Ash'ari, are of the obligation of what cannot be borne, because all the commanded acts are connected to acts which, according to al-Ash'ari, are not within the power of the obligated person. So he is commanded to pray, but he has no power over it. Allah only grants him the power at the time of the will to act, when the causes and instruments are sound."

What Imam al-Haramayn imposed upon al-Ash'ari is a false imposition, because what is meant by what cannot be borne is that which the apparent power of the servant does not reach, which is expressed by acquisition, due to the clear distinction between outward conditions and the hidden realities in the reality of the matter. Likewise, there is no sense in including what Allah knows will not occur, such as commanding Abu Jahl to believe while Allah knows that he will not believe, in the matter of obligation to what cannot be borne or to the impossible, because that knowledge of Allah has not been revealed to anyone. It was objected that the Prophet ﷺ invited Abu Lahab to Islam, while Allah knew that he would not accept it, as indicated by His words ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1] up to His words ﴿He will burn in a fire of blazing flame﴾ [al-Masad: 3]. It may be said that after the revelation of this verse he was not addressed with a demand for faith, but he was addressed before that, and thereby we are spared from saying that he was outside the call, and from saying that he was addressed after the revelation of the verse.

This verse requires that the obligation of what cannot be borne does not occur in the Sacred Law, according to what is customary in human will and capacities, not according to the mystery of predestination and the inquiry into the reality of created power. Yes, a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists) is derived from it.

His words ﴿It shall have what it has earned and it shall bear what it has merited﴾ are a circumstantial clause (hal) from "soul" (nafs), to explain the manner of the capacity with which the soul is charged. That is: if it brings good, its benefit is for it, and if it brings evil, its harm is upon it. This division is produced by the connection through the preposition (al-lam) once and through (ʿala) another time. As for "kasabat" and "iktasabat," they have one meaning in Arabic speech, because the reflexive sense in "iktasaba" is not in its usual pattern. He used "kasaba" once here and "iktasaba" another time for variety and to avoid repeating the same word, as Dhu al-Rummah did in his verse:

"A hunter of game, hungry for his quarry, found his father in that gaining, gaining."

And al-Nabigha's line:

"So I carried Barrah, and you carried Fujar."

The more common and famous form was mentioned first, then it was repeated with its reflexive counterpart. The choice of the verb whose base indicates reflexive action may also be an indication that evil deeds are commanded by Satan, so the soul complies and obeys him, and that is a dislike from Allah toward people for sins. The verb indicating the soul's choice for good deeds was selected as an indication that Allah drives people toward it by their innate nature. It occurs in al-Kashshaf that the reflexive verb, because it indicates effort and striving, and evil is something the soul desires, so it strives to obtain it, thus the action is expressed by iktisab.

What is meant by "what it has merited" (ma iktasabat) is evil deeds. For this reason some exegetes thought that kasb is attaining good and iktisab is attaining evil. This is contrary to the careful analysis, for the Qur'an has ﴿And no soul earns [kasb] except against itself﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and ﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong: Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn [taksibun]?﴾ [Yunus: 52]. It has been said that "iktasaba," when combined with "kasaba," is specified to the act in which there is effort, but the expression "iktasaba" has not come in reference to doing good.

In this verse there is a fine basis for Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari in calling the servant's ability an acquisition (kasb) and an acquiring (iktisab). For Allah described Himself with power, and did not describe the servants with power, nor did He attribute to them the verb "qadara" (to have power). Rather, He attributed acquisition to them. This is a position that brings together the conflicting matters and fulfills the attribution of acts to the servants, along with courtesy by not affirming the attribute of power for the servants. It has been said that the first to use the word kasb was al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Najjar, head of the Najjariyyah sect of the Jabriyyah, who was a contemporary of al-Nazzam in the third century. But al-Ash'ari became famous for it, to the extent that the students said, describing a hidden matter: "More subtle than the acquisition of al-Ash'ari."

The definition of acquisition according to al-Ash'ari is: a state of the servant accompanied by Allah's creation of an act connected to it. Imam al-Razi defined it as an attribute that arises through the servant's power for his act, which occurs through the power of Allah. There are other definitions of acquisition.

The essential meaning of acquisition and what led to affirming it is this: since it has been established that Allah is capable of all beings outside the servant's choice, it is necessary to affirm the generality of His power over everything, lest the power of Allah not extend to some beings, in application of the proofs indicating that Allah is capable of all things and that He is the creator of all things. There is no proof that specifies the generality of these proofs, so this generality must be applied. Then, since it is not permissible to claim that the servant is compelled in his acts, because of the necessary difference between involuntary acts, such as the trembling of one who shakes, and voluntary acts,

(Page 139)

كَحَرَكَةِ الماشِي والقاتِلِ، ورَعْيًا لِحَقِيقَةِ التَّكالِيفِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ لِلْعِبادِ لِئَلّا يَكُونَ التَّكْلِيفُ عَبَثًا، ولِحَقِّيَّةِ الوَعْدِ والوَعِيدِ لِئَلّا يَكُونا باطِلًا، تَعَيَّنَ أنْ تَكُونَ لِلْعَبْدِ حالَةٌ تُمَكِّنُهُ مِن فِعْلِ ما يُرِيدُ فِعْلَهُ، وتَرْكِ ما يُرِيدُ تَرْكَهُ، وهي مَيْلُهُ إلى الفِعْلِ أوِ التَّرْكِ. فَهَذِهِ الحالَةُ سَمّاها الأشْعَرِيُّ (al-Ash'ari) الِاسْتِطاعَةَ، وسَمّاها كَسْبًا (kasb، أي الاكتساب)، وقالَ: إنَّها تَتَعَلَّقُ بِالفِعْلِ، فَإذا تَعَلَّقَتْ بِهِ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ الفِعْلَ الَّذِي مالَ إلَيْهِ على الصُّورَةِ الَّتِي اسْتَحْضَرَها ومالَ إلَيْها.

وتَقْدِيمُ المَجْرُورَيْنِ في الآيَةِ لِقَصْدِ الِاخْتِصاصِ، أيْ لا يَلْحَقُ غَيْرَها شَيْءٌ، ولا يَلْحَقُها شَيْءٌ مِن فِعْلِ غَيْرِها. وكَأنَّ هَذا إبْطالٌ لِما كانُوا عَلَيْهِ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ: مِن اعْتِقادِ شَفاعَةِ الآلِهَةِ لَهم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ.

وتَمَسَّكَ بِهَذِهِ الآيَةِ مَن رَأى أنَّ الأعْمالَ لا تَقْبَلُ النِّيابَةَ في الثَّوابِ والعِقابِ، إلّا إذا كانَ لِلْفاعِلِ أثَرٌ في عَمَلِ غَيْرِهِ. فَفي الحَدِيثِ: «إذا ماتَ ابْنُ آدَمَ انْقَطَعَ عَمَلُهُ إلّا مِن ثَلاثٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جارِيَةٍ، وعِلْمٍ بَثَّهُ في صُدُورِ الرِّجالِ، ووَلَدٍ صالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ»، وفي الحَدِيثِ: «ما مِن نَفْسٍ تُقْتَلُ ظُلْمًا إلّا كانَ على ابْنِ آدَمَ الأوَّلِ كِفْلٌ مِن دَمِها، ذَلِكَ لِأنَّهُ أوَّلُ مَن سَنَّ القَتْلَ»، وفي الحَدِيثِ: «مَن سَنَّ سُنَّةً حَسَنَةً فَلَهُ أجْرُها وأجْرُ مَن عَمِلَ بِها إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ، ومَن سَنَّ سُنَّةً سَيِّئَةً فَعَلَيْهِ وِزْرُها ووِزْرُ مَن عَمِلَ بِها إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ».

* * *

﴿رَبَّنا لا تُؤاخِذْنا إنْ نَسِينا أوْ أخْطَأْنا رَبَّنا ولا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنا إصْرًا كَما حَمَلْتَهُ عَلى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنا رَبَّنا ولا تُحَمِّلْنا ما لا طاقَةَ لَنا بِهِ واعْفُ عَنّا واغْفِرْ لَنا وارْحَمْنا أنْتَ مَوْلانا فانْصُرْنا عَلى القَوْمِ الكافِرِينَ﴾.

يَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ هَذا الدُّعاءُ مَحْكِيًّا مِن قَوْلِ المُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: ﴿سَمِعْنا وأطَعْنا﴾ [البقرة: ٢٨٥]، بِأنِ اتَّبَعُوا القَبُولَ والرِّضا، فَتَوَجَّهُوا إلى طَلَبِ الجَزاءِ ومُناجاةِ اللَّهِ تَعالى. واخْتِيارُ حِكايَةِ هَذا عَنْهم في آخِرِ السُّورَةِ تَكْمِلَةٌ لِلْإيذانِ بِانْتِهائِها. ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ تَلْقِينًا مِن جانِبِ اللَّهِ تَعالى إيّاهم بِأنْ يَقُولُوا هَذا الدُّعاءَ، مِثْلَ ما لُقِّنُوا التَّحْمِيدَ في سُورَةِ الفاتِحَةِ، فَيَكُونُ

[صفحة ١٤٠]

التَّقْدِيرُ: قُولُوا: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تُؤاخِذْنا﴾ إلى آخِرِ السُّورَةِ. إنَّ اللَّهَ بَعْدَ أنْ قَرَّرَ لَهم أنَّهُ لا يُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إلّا وُسْعَها، لَقَّنَهم مُناجاةً بِدَعَواتٍ هي مِن آثارِ انْتِفاءِ التَّكْلِيفِ بِما لَيْسَ في الوُسْعِ. والمُرادُ مِنَ الدُّعاءِ بِهِ طَلَبُ الدَّوامِ على ذَلِكَ، لِئَلّا يُنْسَخَ ذَلِكَ مِن جَرّاءِ غَضَبِ اللَّهِ، كَما غَضِبَ على الَّذِينَ قالَ فِيهِمْ: ﴿فَبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّباتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾ [النساء: ١٦٠].

والمُؤاخَذَةُ مُشْتَقَّةٌ مِنَ الأخْذِ بِمَعْنى العُقُوبَةِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وكَذَلِكَ أخْذُ رَبِّكَ إذا أخَذَ القُرى وهي ظالِمَةٌ﴾ [هود: ١٠٢]، والمُفاعَلَةُ فِيهِ لِلْمُبالَغَةِ، أيْ: لا تَأْخُذْنا بِالنِّسْيانِ والخَطَأِ.

والمُرادُ ما يَتَرَتَّبُ على النِّسْيانِ والخَطَأِ مِن فِعْلٍ أوْ تَرْكٍ لا يُرْضِيانِ اللَّهَ تَعالى.

فَهَذِهِ دَعْوَةٌ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ دَعَوْها قَبْلَ أنْ يَعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ رَفَعَ عَنْهم ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إلّا وُسْعَها﴾، وقَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): «رُفِعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي الخَطَأُ والنِّسْيانُ وما اسْتُكْرِهُوا عَلَيْهِ»، وفي رِوايَةٍ: «وُضِعَ»، رَواهُ ابْنُ ماجَهْ (Ibn Majah)، وتَكَلَّمَ العُلَماءُ في صِحَّتِهِ، وقَدْ حَسَّنَهُ النَّوَوِيُّ (al-Nawawi)، وأنْكَرَهُ أحْمَدُ (Ahmad)، ومَعْناهُ صَحِيحٌ في غَيْرِ ما يَرْجِعُ إلى خِطابِ الوَضْعِ (khitab al-wad'، أي الحكم الوضعي المتعلق بالأسباب والشروط والموانع)، فالمَعْنى: رَفَعَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمُ المُؤاخَذَةَ، فَبَقِيَتِ المُؤاخَذَةُ بِالإتْلافِ والغَراماتِ. ولِذَلِكَ جاءَ في هَذِهِ الدَّعْوَةِ ﴿لا تُؤاخِذْنا﴾، أيْ: لا تُؤاخِذْنا بِالعِقابِ على فِعْلٍ: نِسْيانٍ أوْ خَطَأٍ. فَلا يَرِدُ إشْكالُ الدُّعاءِ بِما عُلِمَ حُصُولُهُ، حَتّى نَحْتاجَ إلى تَأْوِيلِ الآيَةِ بِأنَّ المُرادَ بِالنِّسْيانِ والخَطَأِ سَبَبُهُما، وهو التَّفْرِيطُ والإغْفالُ، كَما في الكَشّافِ (al-Kashshaf، للزمخشري).

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿رَبَّنا ولا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنا إصْرًا﴾ إلخ، فَصْلٌ بَيْنَ الجُمْلَتَيْنِ المُتَعاطِفَتَيْنِ بِإعادَةِ النِّداءِ، مَعَ أنَّهُ مُسْتَغْنًى عَنْهُ، لِأنَّ مُخاطَبَةَ المُنادى مُغْنِيَةٌ عَنْ إعادَةِ النِّداءِ، لَكِنْ قُصِدَ مِن إعادَتِهِ إظْهارُ التَّذَلُّلِ. والحَمْلُ مَجازٌ في التَّكْلِيفِ بِأمْرٍ شَدِيدٍ يَثْقُلُ على النَّفْسِ، وهو مُناسِبٌ لِاسْتِعارَةِ الإصْرِ.

وأصْلُ مَعْنى الإصْرِ ما يُؤْصَرُ بِهِ، أيْ يُرْبَطُ، وتُعْقَدُ بِهِ الأشْياءُ، ويُقالُ لَهُ: الإصارُ بِكَسْرِ الهَمْزَةِ. ثُمَّ اسْتُعْمِلَ مَجازًا في العَهْدِ والمِيثاقِ المُؤَكَّدِ فِيما يَصْعُبُ الوَفاءُ بِهِ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ في آلِ عِمْرانَ: (﴿قالَ أقْرَرْتُمْ وأخَذْتُمْ عَلى ذَلِكم إصْرِي﴾ [آل عمران: ٨١])، وأُطْلِقَ أيْضًا عَلى ما يَثْقُلُ عَمَلُهُ والِامْتِثالُ فِيهِ، وبِذَلِكَ فَسَّرَهُ الزَّجّاجُ (al-Zajjaj) والزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ هُنا، وفي قَوْلِهِ، في

[صفحة ١٤١]

سُورَةِ الأعْرافِ: ﴿ويَضَعُ عَنْهم إصْرَهُمْ﴾ [الأعراف: ١٥٧]، وهو المَقْصُودُ هُنا. ومِن ثَمَّ حَسُنَتِ اسْتِعارَةُ الحَمْلِ لِلتَّكْلِيفِ، لِأنَّ الحَمْلَ يُناسِبُ الثِّقَلَ، فَيَكُونُ قَوْلُهُ ﴿ولا تَحْمِلْ﴾ تَرْشِيحًا مُسْتَعارًا لِمُلائِمِ المُشَبَّهِ بِهِ. وعَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ (Ibn 'Abbas) رضي الله عنهما: ﴿ولا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنا إصْرًا﴾ عَهْدًا لا نَفِي بِهِ، ونُعَذَّبُ بِتَرْكِهِ ونَقْضِهِ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿كَما حَمَلْتَهُ عَلى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنا﴾ صِفَةٌ لِـ"إصْرًا"، أيْ: عَهْدًا مِنَ الدِّينِ، كالعَهْدِ الَّذِي كُلِّفَ بِهِ مَن قَبْلَنا في المَشَقَّةِ، مِثْلَ ما كُلِّفَ بِهِ بَعْضُ الأُمَمِ الماضِيَةِ مِنَ الأحْكامِ الشّاقَّةِ، مِثْلِ أمْرِ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ بِتِيهِ أرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً، وبِصِفاتٍ في البَقَرَةِ الَّتِي أُمِرُوا بِذَبْحِها نادِرَةٍ، ونَحْوِ ذَلِكَ. وكُلُّ ذَلِكَ تَأْدِيبٌ لَهم على مُخالَفاتٍ، وعَلى قِلَّةِ اهْتِبالٍ بِأوامِرِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ إلَيْهِمْ. قالَ تَعالى في صِفَةِ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ): ﴿ويَضَعُ عَنْهم إصْرَهُمْ﴾ [الأعراف: ١٥٧].

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿رَبَّنا ولا تُحَمِّلْنا ما لا طاقَةَ لَنا بِهِ﴾، أيْ: ما لا نَسْتَطِيعُ حَمْلَهُ مِنَ العُقُوباتِ، والتَّضْعِيفُ فِيهِ لِلتَّعْدِيَةِ. وقِيلَ: هَذا دُعاءٌ بِمُعافاتِهِمْ مِنَ التَّكالِيفِ الشَّدِيدَةِ، والَّذِي قَبْلَهُ دُعاءٌ بِمُعافاتِهِمْ مِنَ العُقُوباتِ الَّتِي عُوقِبَتْ بِها الأُمَمُ. والطّاقَةُ في الأصْلِ الإطاقَةُ، خُفِّفَتْ بِحَذْفِ الهَمْزَةِ، كَما قالُوا: جابَةٌ وإجابَةٌ، وطاعَةٌ وإطاعَةٌ.

والقَوْلُ في هَذَيْنِ الدُّعاءَيْنِ كالقَوْلِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تُؤاخِذْنا﴾.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿واعْفُ عَنّا واغْفِرْ لَنا﴾ لَمْ يُؤْتَ مَعَ هَذِهِ الدَّعَواتِ بِقَوْلِهِ "رَبَّنا"، إمّا لِأنَّهُ تَكَرَّرَ ثَلاثَ مَرّاتٍ، والعَرَبُ تَكْرَهُ تَكْرِيرَ اللَّفْظِ أكْثَرَ مِن ثَلاثِ مَرّاتٍ إلّا في مَقامِ التَّهْوِيلِ، وإمّا لِأنَّ تِلْكَ الدَّعَواتِ المُقْتَرِنَةَ بِقَوْلِهِ "رَبَّنا" فُرُوعٌ لِهَذِهِ الدَّعَواتِ الثَّلاثِ، فَإنِ اسْتُجِيبَتْ تِلْكَ حَصَلَتْ إجابَةُ هَذِهِ بِالأوْلى، فَإنَّ العَفْوَ أصْلٌ لِعَدَمِ المُؤاخَذَةِ، والمَغْفِرَةَ أصْلٌ لِرَفْعِ المَشَقَّةِ، والرَّحْمَةَ أصْلٌ لِعَدَمِ العُقُوبَةِ الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ والأُخْرَوِيَّةِ، فَلَمّا كانَ تَعْمِيمًا بَعْدَ تَخْصِيصٍ كانَ كَأنَّهُ دُعاءٌ واحِدٌ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿أنْتَ مَوْلانا﴾ فَصَلَهُ لِأنَّهُ كالعِلَّةِ لِلدَّعَواتِ الماضِيَةِ، أيْ: دَعَوْناكَ ورَجَوْنا مِنكَ ذَلِكَ لِأنَّكَ مَوْلانا، ومِن شَأْنِ المَوْلى الرِّفْقُ بِالمَمْلُوكِ، ولِيَكُونَ هَذا أيْضًا كالمُقَدِّمَةِ لِلدَّعْوَةِ الآتِيَةِ.

[صفحة ١٤٢]

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فانْصُرْنا عَلى القَوْمِ الكافِرِينَ﴾ جِيءَ فِيهِ بِالفاءِ لِلتَّفْرِيعِ عَنْ كَوْنِهِ مَوْلًى، لِأنَّ شَأْنَ المَوْلى أنْ يَنْصُرَ مَوْلاهُ. ومِن هُنا يَظْهَرُ مَوْقِعُ التَّعْجِيبِ والتَّحْسِيرِ في قَوْلِ مُرَّةَ بْنِ عَدّاءٍ الفَقْعَسِيِّ (Murrah ibn 'Adda al-Faqʻasi):

رَأيْتُ مَوالِيَ الأُلى يَخْذُلُونَنِي على حَدَثانِ الدَّهْرِ إذْ يَتَقَلَّبُ

وفِي التَّفْرِيعِ بِالفاءِ إيذانٌ بِتَأْكِيدِ طَلَبِ إجابَةِ الدُّعاءِ بِالنَّصْرِ، لِأنَّهم جَعَلُوهُ مُرَتَّبًا على وصْفٍ مُحَقَّقٍ، وهو وِلايَةُ اللَّهِ تَعالى المُؤْمِنِينَ، قالَ تَعالى: ﴿اللَّهُ ولِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [البقرة: ٢٥٧]. وفي حَدِيثِ «يَوْمِ أُحُدٍ لَمّا قالَ أبُو سُفْيانَ (Abu Sufyan): لَنا العُزّى ولا عُزّى لَكم. قالَ النَّبِيءُ (ﷺ): أجِيبُوهُ: اللَّهُ مَوْلانا ولا مَوْلى لَكم». ووَجْهُ الِاهْتِمامِ بِهَذِهِ الدَّعْوَةِ أنَّها دَعْوَةٌ جامِعَةٌ لِخَيْرَيِ الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ، لِأنَّهم إذا نُصِرُوا على العَدُوِّ، فَقَدْ طابَ عَيْشُهم وظَهَرَ دِينُهم، وسَلِمُوا مِنَ الفِتْنَةِ، ودَخَلَ النّاسُ فِيهِ أفْواجًا.

فِي الصَّحِيحِ، عَنْ أبِي مَسْعُودٍ الأنْصارِيِّ البَدْرِيِّ (Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari al-Badri): أنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) قالَ: «مَن قَرَأ الآيَتَيْنِ مِن آخِرِ سُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ في لَيْلَةٍ كَفَتاهُ»، وهُما مِن قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِما أُنْزِلَ إلَيْهِ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾ [البقرة: ٢٨٥] إلى آخِرِ السُّورَةِ. قِيلَ: مَعْناهُ كَفَتاهُ عَنْ قِيامِ اللَّيْلِ، فَيَكُونُ مَعْنى "مَن قَرَأ" مَن صَلّى بِهِما. وقِيلَ: مَعْناهُ كَفَتاهُ بَرَكَةً وتَعَوُّذًا مِنَ الشَّياطِينِ والمَضارِّ، ولَعَلَّ كِلا الِاحْتِمالَيْنِ مُرادٌ.

* * *

[صفحة ١٤٣]

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ. سُورَةُ آلِ عِمْرانَ. سُمِّيَتْ هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ، في كَلامِ النَّبِيءِ (ﷺ) وكَلامِ الصَّحابَةِ: سُورَةَ آلِ عِمْرانَ. فَفي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ أبِي أُمامَةَ قالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ: «اقْرَءُوا الزَّهْراوَيْنِ: البَقَرَةَ وآلَ عِمْرانَ». وفِيهِ عَنِ النَّوّاسِ بْنِ سَمْعانَ (al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an) قالَ: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيءَ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ: «يُؤْتى بِالقُرْآنِ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ، تَقْدُمُهُ سُورَةُ البَقَرَةِ وآلِ عِمْرانَ». ورَوى الدّارِمِيُّ (al-Darimi) في مُسْنَدِهِ: أنَّ عُثْمانَ بْنَ عَفّانَ (رضي الله عنه) قالَ: مَن قَرَأ سُورَةَ آلِ عِمْرانَ في لَيْلَةٍ كُتِبَ لَهُ قِيامُ لَيْلَةٍ. وسَمّاها ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، في حَدِيثِهِ في الصَّحِيحِ، قالَ: «بِتُّ في بَيْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) فَنامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ حَتّى إذا كانَ نِصْفُ اللَّيْلِ أوْ قَبْلَهُ بِقَلِيلٍ أوْ بَعْدَهُ بِقَلِيلٍ اسْتَيْقَظَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، فَقَرَأ الآياتِ مِن آخِرِ سُورَةِ آلِ عِمْرانَ». ووَجْهُ تَسْمِيَتِها بِسُورَةِ آلِ عِمْرانَ أنَّها ذُكِرَتْ فِيها فَضائِلُ آلِ عِمْرانَ، وهو عِمْرانُ بْنُ ماتانَ (Imran ibn Matan) أبُو مَرْيَمَ، وآلُهُ هم زَوْجُهُ حَنَّةُ، وأُخْتُها زَوْجَةُ زَكَرِيّاءَ النَّبِيءِ (Zakariyya)، وزَكَرِيّاءُ كافِلُ مَرْيَمَ، إذْ كانَ أبُوها عِمْرانُ قَدْ تُوُفِّيَ وتَرَكَها حَمْلًا، فَكَفَلَها زَوْجُ خالَتِها.

ووَصَفَها رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) بِالزَّهْراءِ في حَدِيثِ أبِي أُمامَةَ المُتَقَدِّمِ.

وذَكَرَ الألُوسِيُّ (al-Alusi) أنَّها تُسَمّى الأمانَ، والكَنْزَ، والمُجادِلَةَ، وسُورَةَ الِاسْتِغْفارِ. ولَمْ أرَهُ لِغَيْرِهِ، ولَعَلَّهُ اقْتَبَسَ ذَلِكَ مِن أوْصافٍ وُصِفَتْ بِها هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ، مِمّا ساقَهُ القُرْطُبِيُّ (al-Qurtubi) في المَسْألَةِ الثّالِثَةِ والرّابِعَةِ مِن تَفْسِيرِ أوَّلِ السُّورَةِ.

وهَذِهِ السُّورَةُ نَزَلَتْ بِالمَدِينَةِ بِالِاتِّفاقِ، بَعْدَ سُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ. فَقِيلَ: إنَّها ثانِيَةٌ لِسُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ، على أنَّ البَقَرَةَ أوَّلُ سُورَةٍ نَزَلَتْ بِالمَدِينَةِ. وقِيلَ: نَزَلَتْ بِالمَدِينَةِ سُورَةُ المُطَفِّفِينَ أوَّلًا، ثُمَّ البَقَرَةُ، ثُمَّ نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ آلِ عِمْرانَ، ثُمَّ نَزَلَتِ الأنْفالُ في وقْعَةِ بَدْرٍ. وهَذا يَقْتَضِي أنَّ سُورَةَ آلِ عِمْرانَ نَزَلَتْ قَبْلَ وقْعَةِ بَدْرٍ، لِلِاتِّفاقِ على أنَّ الأنْفالَ نَزَلَتْ في

[صفحة ١٤٤]

وقْعَةِ بَدْرٍ. ويُبْعِدُ ذَلِكَ أنَّ سُورَةَ آلِ عِمْرانَ اشْتَمَلَتْ على التَّذْكِيرِ بِنَصْرِ المُسْلِمِينَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ، وأنَّ فِيها ذِكْرَ يَوْمِ أُحُدٍ، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ بَعْضُها نَزَلَ مُتَأخِّرًا. وذَكَرَ الواحِدِيُّ (al-Wahidi) في أسْبابِ النُّزُولِ، عَنِ المُفَسِّرِينَ، أنَّ أوَّلَ هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ونَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ [البقرة: ١٣٦] نَزَلَ بِسَبَبِ وفْدِ نَجْرانَ (Najran)، وهو وفْدُ السَّيِّدِ والعاقِبِ، أيْ سَنَةَ اثْنَتَيْنِ مِنَ الهِجْرَةِ. ومِنَ العُلَماءِ مَن قالُوا: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ آلِ عِمْرانَ بَعْدَ سُورَةِ الأنْفالِ، وكانَ نُزُولُها في وقْعَةِ أُحُدٍ، أيْ شَوّالٍ سَنَةَ ثَلاثٍ، وهَذا أقْرَبُ، فَقَدِ اتَّفَقَ المُفَسِّرُونَ على أنَّ قَوْلَهُ تَعالى: ﴿وإذْ غَدَوْتَ مِن أهْلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ المُؤْمِنِينَ مَقاعِدَ لِلْقِتالِ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٢١] أنَّهُ قِتالُ يَوْمِ أُحُدٍ. وكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وما مُحَمَّدٌ إلّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ أفَإنْ ماتَ أوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ على أعْقابِكُمْ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٤٤]، فَإنَّهُ مُشِيرٌ إلى الإرْجافِ يَوْمَ أُحُدٍ بِقَتْلِ النَّبِيءِ (ﷺ).

The passage may also be that its first part was revealed after al-Baqarah, up to the end of what the hadith of the delegation of Najran alludes to. That is about eighty verses from its beginning up to His saying ﴿And when you set out from your family﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 121]. This was said by al-Qurṭubī at the beginning of the surah, and in his commentary on His saying ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Book﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 79], the verse. We have already stated at the beginning of Sūrat al-Fātiḥah that it is possible for several surahs to be revealed within one period. So the meaning of their saying, "Surah such-and-such was revealed after surah such-and-such," is not that the one counted as revealed after the other had its revelation begun after the other's revelation was completed. Rather, the intended meaning is that its revelation began after the beginning of the revelation of the one that preceded it.

This surah has been counted as the forty-eighth in the enumeration of the surahs of the Qur'an.

The number of its verses is two hundred according to the count of the majority, and according to the people of counting (ahl al-ʿadad) in Syria it is one hundred and ninety-nine.

This surah includes, among its themes: the opening with the exalting of the Qur'an and of Muḥammad (ﷺ); the division of the verses of the Qur'an; the levels of understanding in receiving them; the exalting of the excellence of Islam and that no religion equals it; that no religion is accepted by God after the appearance of Islam other than Islam; the exalting of the Torah and the Gospel, with an allusion that they were sent down before the Qur'an as a preparation for this religion, so it is not right for people to disbelieve in it; the description of the proofs of the divinity of God, the Exalted, and His uniqueness; the refutation of the error of those who took gods besides God, whether they associated partners with Him or attributed sons to Him; the warning to the polytheists that their affair is heading toward decline, and that the luxury they are in should not deceive them, and that what is prepared for the believers is better than that; the warning to them of the loss of their authority; then the praise of ʿĪsā (Jesus), peace be upon him, and his family; the mention of the miracle of his coming into existence; that he is a creature of God; the mention of those who truly believed in him; the refutation of the divinity of ʿĪsā; and from this it led to the matter of the delegation of Najran and their obstinacy. Then the argument with the People of the Two Books concerning the reality of the ḥanīfiyyah (the pure monotheistic faith of Abraham), and that they are far removed from it; and the covenant that God took from all the messengers: that they should believe in the final Messenger. And that God made the Kaʿbah the first House established for mankind, and He has restored to it the upright religion as He began it there, and He made its pilgrimage obligatory upon the believers. He also exposed the errors of the Jews, the evil of their statements, their fabrication in their religion, and their concealment of what was revealed to them. He reminded the Muslims of His blessing upon them through the religion of Islam, commanded them to unity and harmony, reminded them of their former evil state in the Jāhiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance), and made light for them the support given to their opponents among the People of the Book and the polytheists. He warned them to beware of their scheming and the scheming of those who displayed Islam and then reverted to disbelief, and they became an example for distinguishing the wicked from the good. He commanded them to take pride in themselves, to be patient in enduring hardships, afflictions and the harm of the enemy, and promised them victory, support, and the casting of terror from them into the hearts of their enemies in return. Then He reminded them of the Day of Uḥud and the Day of Badr, and set forth examples from what occurred in them. He honored the martyrs among the Muslims, and commanded the Muslims to virtuous deeds: spending wealth to assist the community, good conduct, excellent works, and abandoning miserliness; and He condemned usury. The surah concludes with verses of reflection upon the dominion (malakūt) of God.

You have already learned that the cause of the revelation of this surah was the matter of the delegation of Najran from the lands of Yemen.

The delegation of Najran were people from Najran who had heard of the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ). The people of Najran adhered to Christianity, and they were among the most sincere of the Arabs in their adherence to the religion of the Messiah. Among them were famous monks, and they had set up a Kaʿbah for Christianity in their land, which is the one the poet al-Aʿshā referred to when he praised them, saying:

"So the Kaʿbah of Najrān is an obligation upon you,
until you kneel your camels at its doors."

A delegation from them gathered, led by al-ʿĀqib, in which there were sixty men, and his name was ʿAbd al-Masīḥ, and he was the leader of the delegation. With him was al-Sayyid, whose name was al-Ayham, who was the thimāl (protector and support) of the people, the one in charge of managing the delegation, its adviser, and the man of counsel among them. Among them also was Abū Ḥārithah ibn ʿAlqamah al-Bakrī, who was their bishop, the head of their place of study (midrās), and the guardian of their religion. Among them was also the brother of Abū Ḥārithah, who was not from the people of Najran, but he held a high rank: the kings of Rome had honored him and given him patronage. They met the Prophet (ﷺ) and he argued with them about their religion and about the question of the divinity of the Messiah. When the proof was established against them, they persisted in their disbelief and obstinately refused. The Prophet (ﷺ) then called them to mubāhalah (mutual invocation of divine curse upon the liars). They agreed, then they were overawed by it, withdrew from it, and returned to their homelands. About eighty-some verses from the beginning of this surah were revealed concerning them, as is found in the Sīrah of Ibn Hishām from Ibn Isḥāq. This was mentioned by al-Wāḥidī and al-Fakhr (al-Rāzī). So whoever among the people of biography thinks that the delegation of Najran came in the year nine has erred in an error that was carried to him by the fame of the year nine as the "year of the delegations." The consensus is that Sūrat Āl ʿImrān is among the earliest Medinan surahs, and the preponderant view that it was revealed concerning the delegation of Najran indicates that the delegation of Najran came before the year of the delegations.
